```
=== writeup ===
10th Place Solution — NVIDIA Nemotron Model Reasoning Challenge

NVIDIA Nemotron Model Reasoning Challenge


Solution Writeup · 10th place · Jun 18, 2026

Many thanks to NVIDIA and the Kaggle staff for organizing the Nemotron Model Reasoning
Challenge, and congratulations to everyone who placed. This was a great competition to work
on, and I learned a lot from building a fully deterministic data pipeline around a single base
model.




Overview
Our solution was based on deterministic program-generated reasoning traces rather than LLM
distillation. For each task category, we built symbolic reasoners that derive answers from the
prompt alone, then fine-tuned a single base model to imitate those reasoning procedures.

   •   Method
          o Program-based deterministic reasoners generate Chain-of-Thought (CoT) traces
             for synthetic problems across 9 task categories.
          o Each reasoner re-derives the answer from the prompt alone. It never reads the
             ground-truth answer and emits a step-by-step CoT ending in \boxed{answer}.
          o We then SFT a single base model with LoRA on those traces so it learns the
             reasoning procedure, not just the answer.
   •   Base model
           o    nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF16
                30B Mixture-of-Experts, approximately 3B active parameters.
   •   Scores
           o    Public LB: 0.860
           o    Private LB: 0.880
           o    Placement: 10th

The main lesson was that the final score was mostly limited by the quality and coverage of the
deterministic teachers. Once the traces were clean, compact, and consistent, the model could
imitate them surprisingly well.




Core idea — Synthetic data + procedure learning
Each category has a program-based deterministic reasoner that re-derives the answer from the
prompt alone. The stored answer is never used during trace generation. The generated trace
explains the procedure step by step and ends with \boxed{answer}.

The corpus tokenizes each example with the chat template, masks the prompt tokens with
mask=0, and trains only on the completion tokens with mask=1. This lets the LoRA adapter learn
the generated reasoning procedure rather than only the final answer.

A useful working assumption was that, given clean and consistent traces, SFT could imitate the
teacher reasoner closely. Therefore, validation accuracy was largely bounded by the reasoner's
own oracle accuracy. The main lever was improving the coverage and learnability of the
generated traces, rather than relying on SFT hyperparameter tricks.




Oracle coverage by category
         Category       Found Total Accuracy
bit_manipulation        1582 1602 98.8%
cipher                  1576 1576 100.0%
cryptarithm_deduce      59    659 9.0%
cryptarithm_guess       13    164 7.9%
equation_numeric_deduce 555 596 93.1%
equation_numeric_guess 56     136 41.2%
gravity                 1597 1597 100.0%
numeral                 1576 1576 100.0%
unit_conversion         1594 1594 100.0%
TOTAL                   8608 9500 90.6%



Main reasoner improvements
The largest gain came from bit_manipulation, where the reasoner was rewritten to match the
true task structure more closely. A smaller but important improvement came from
equation_numeric, where candidate ordering and unseen-operator guessing were improved
using corpus statistics.




bit_manipulation trace update
The main reasoner change in this solution was to rewrite the bit_manipulation generator from
a per-bit logical-operation matcher into a rotate/shift key-table reasoner.
This improved reasoner oracle accuracy from 1364/1602 = 85.14% to 1582/1602 = 98.75%,
while replacing long, loop-prone traces with shorter derivations that were easier for the model to
copy.

Background

The original generator modeled every output bit as a logical operation over fixed input columns.
For each output column, it searched candidate families such as Identity, NOT, constant 0,
constant 1, AND, OR, XOR, AND-NOT, OR-NOT, and XOR-NOT.

It then found operand pairs whose columns reproduced the output, built left and right stride runs,
truncated them to eight bits, and filled the middle slots by a category vote.

This representation did not match the actual task structure well. The underlying transform was a
rotate-and-shift composition rather than arbitrary per-bit boolean logic over fixed columns. As a
result, many problems could not be expressed well by the old family search, which limited the
oracle ceiling to 1364/1602 = 85.14%.

The traces were also long and enumeration-heavy, with repeated Left, Right, Best, Truncated,
Tentative, Preferred, and Matched sections. These traces were difficult for the model to
imitate reliably and sometimes encouraged runaway generation loops.

Key-table reasoner

The reasoner was redesigned around the rule that generates the data:

out[i] = F(rotl(x, a)[i], shl(x, b)[i], shr(x, c)[i])
content_copy

Here:

   •    rotl is the input rotated left by a, where a ranges from 0 to 7.
   •    shl is the input shifted left by b, where b ranges from 1 to 7 with zero fill.
   •    shr is the input shifted right by c, where c ranges from 1 to 7 with zero fill.
   •    F is a shared 3-input boolean function used for every bit.

Instead of naming F, the reasoner reads it from the examples as a key table that maps each 3-bit
key to an output bit.

The offsets (a, b, c) are recovered from boundary bits where one operand is forced to zero. At
bit 0, shr = 0; at bit 7, shl = 0. Therefore, each boundary output column must be a function of
only two input columns. Scanning single columns and column pairs at these boundaries
constrains (a, b) from bit 0 and (a, c) from bit 7.
Each surviving candidate (a, b, c) is then verified against every example. The reasoner
accumulates the key table example by example and rejects a candidate as soon as a conflict
appears. The first candidate whose table covers all keys needed for the question is selected.

Ties and uncovered keys fall back to agreement, where the same prediction must appear twice
and unknown values are filled with 1, or to a per-bit majority vote. The stored answer is never
used during this process.

Trace efficiency

The trace was shortened without changing any answers.

Redundant per-example bit echoes were removed because verification only needs the transposed
columns. The candidate List: enumeration was also removed, since it was the largest source of
long traces and often caused runaway generation loops. The candidate walk now iterates the set
directly.

Additional boundary scans for bits 1 and 6, then bits 2 and 5, are only run when the candidate set
is large. This is gated by a count threshold of _THRESH = 24.

Keys are rendered compactly in key>value form.

Remaining oracle failures

The reasoner still fails on 20/1602 problems.

All 20 problems are expressible within the rotate/shift plus key-table family, so there were no
failures caused by the rule being outside the reasoner's hypothesis class. The remaining failures
come from ambiguity in identifying the rule from the given examples.

Of these 20 failures, 11 are inherently underdetermined. In these cases, the question requires a 3-
bit key that never appears in the examples, leaving a hole in the key table. The reasoner must fill
the missing value through fallback logic such as filling with 1 or using a majority vote, but the
examples do not contain enough information to determine the answer uniquely.

The other 9 failures are candidate-selection errors. In these cases, at least one consistent (a, b,
c) decomposition gives the correct answer, but multiple decompositions are consistent with the
examples. The reasoner's selection order or fallback path chooses a different consistent
candidate, leading to the wrong answer.

Token budget

Not all regenerated traces fit within an 8192-token budget. In total, 1578/1602
bit_manipulation examples were included, meaning 24 examples were dropped and did not
provide training traces.
These excluded cases were mainly heavy examples with candidate explosion.

Result

Reasoner oracle accuracy improved from 1364/1602 = 85.14% to 1582/1602 = 98.75%.

On the validation subset, the reasoner was oracle-correct on 169/169 problems without
introducing regressions.




equation_numeric trace update
equation_numeric asks the model to recover the rule behind an operator glyph ◯ in
expressions such as:

a ◯ b = out
content_copy

The glyph is arbitrary and its meaning changes per problem. There are two subtasks:

   •   deduce — the queried glyph appears in the examples.
   •   guess — the queried glyph does not appear in the examples.

Both changes leave the search core untouched:

   •   deduce — reorder which candidates are tried.
   •   guess — improve unseen-operator prediction using corpus statistics.

Three corpus observations

These observations were verified on the real data.

   1. Operations are frequency-skewed.

       add, mul, sub(a-b), and abs dominate the corpus.

   add           250
   mul           247
   sub(a-b)      233
   abs           159
content_copy

The glyph - maps to signed subtraction 52% of the time, and sub outnumbers neg-abs by
roughly 3:1.
Therefore, frequent and conventional operations should be tried first.

   1. The wrapper is shared across a whole problem.

       Operand reversal, result reversal, and sign formatting were shared across a whole
       problem in 688/688 cases.

       Therefore, solving a single operator can pin the wrapper, which can then be reused for an
       unseen one.

   2. Operations usually do not repeat within a problem.

       Operations did not repeat within a problem in 676/688 cases.

       Therefore, an unseen operator is most likely an unused operation.

deduce — fixing the candidate trial order

For deduce, the main change was to reorder candidates by frequency and to make - try
conventional signed subtraction before absolute difference.

With a single example, several operations can match at once. In that case, trial order alone
decides which operation is accepted.

Baseline — abs tried first:
  97-03 = 94: |97-03| = 94          match      <- accepted
               97-03   = 94         match      <- also correct, skipped
  apply 52-99: |52-99| = 47                    <- wrong

After — '-' tries subtraction first:
  97-03 = 94: 97-03    = 94 match    <- accepted
               |97-03| = 94 match    <- also correct, skipped
  apply 52-99: 52-99 = -47           <- correct
content_copy

Result: deduce oracle improved from 541 to 555, a gain of +14.

guess — rebuilding both axes of the guess

For guess, the queried glyph does not appear in the examples, so the reasoner must infer both:

   1. which operation to use;
   2. which wrapper to apply.

The output has the form:

wrapper(op(a, b))
content_copy
The previous guess reasoner fixed op to absolute difference and only borrowed the wrapper from
the most frequent operator. This gave 21/136 oracle accuracy. We reworked both the operation
choice and the wrapper choice.

A. Choosing the operation

The operation is selected in two steps.

   1. If the glyph has a conventional meaning, use it when available.
           o + → addition
           o - → signed subtraction
           o * → multiplication

       This convention is used only if no seen operator already uses that operation.

   2. Otherwise, choose the first unused operation from the candidate trio:

   addition, absolute difference, multiplication
content_copy

The order follows corpus frequency.

The difference slot here is unsigned absolute difference. For arbitrary glyphs, the result is almost
always non-negative, so the unsigned form gets the sign right more often.

B. Choosing the wrapper

An unseen operator has zero examples, so its wrapper cannot be derived from itself.

Using the observation that the wrapper is shared across a whole problem, the seen operator with
the most examples is solved in full to pin the wrapper. That wrapper is then reused for the unseen
operator.

Skipping this step often leaves the operation right but the answer shifted, for example 4
becoming 04.

Worked examples

 Problem                 Glyph             A seen operator
         Query                                                  Chosen op       New Gold Baseline
   ID                  convention               uses
                                                             mul, convention
1c4861e6     12*91 multiplication         - = abs diff                          993 993 79 ✗
                                                             free
                                                             sub, convention
07aef27f     22-84 subtraction            * = multiply+1                        -62 -62 62 ✗
                                                             free
0c0683c3     79"59 none                   - = abs diff       add, top unused    138 138 20 ✗
Example of the fallback in step A.2:

77+42
content_copy

In this problem, addition and absolute difference are both already in use, so the reasoner chooses
multiplication:

77 × 42 = 3234
content_copy

This is within 1% of the gold answer, 3235.

Result: guess oracle improved from 21/136 to 56/136, a gain of +35.




Training & hyperparameters
       Item                                           Setting
Data scope         Full training data, no OOF exclusion
Token filter       Exclude samples over 8192 tokens
                   Mix self-priority, y-trap bit_manipulation, and dictionary-search cipher
Priority
                   at 2x each
LoRA rank          32
LoRA alpha         128, so lora_alpha / r = 4
LoRA dropout       0.0
Target modules     q_proj, k_proj, v_proj, o_proj, in_proj, out_proj, up_proj, down_proj
lm_head LoRA       Enabled. lm_head is added to the target modules above
max_seq_length     8192
Learning rate      2e-4
Scheduler          lr_scheduler_type=linear, warmup_ratio=0.0
Epochs             2
Effective batch
                   32
size
Sampling           Stratified sampling

Priority samples were examples or demos associated with known fragile failure modes. They
were duplicated at 2x so the model saw those traces more often without overwhelming the
original distribution.




Additional techniques
Add low-logprob problems and retrain

Low-logprob problems were added or duplicated in the training corpus as priority samples, then
SFT was run again.

This was not just a way to increase data volume. It was a way to re-expose traces that the model
tended to forget, or traces where boundary decisions were fragile.

Demos for failure patterns, such as candidate acceptance/suppression in bit_manipulation and
dictionary search in cipher, were mixed in with the same idea. The objective was to repeatedly
train the reasoning steps the model was weak at and compress them into a single adapter.

Raising the LoRA alpha

To make the adapter follow the deterministic CoT more strongly, the final recipe used:

lora_alpha / r = 4
content_copy

This improved CV.




Validation strategy
Held-out split

950 problems were excluded from training and used as a fixed validation set. Accuracy was
tracked per category.

Oracle ceiling and fidelity

Since the model imitates the reasoner, we compared model accuracy against the reasoner's own
oracle accuracy and monitored how closely the model reached that ceiling.

This made it easier to separate two failure modes:

   1. the reasoner itself produced the wrong answer;
   2. the model failed to imitate a correct trace.

Learnability analysis

Per-example and per-epoch log probabilities were used to identify examples and trace steps that
were difficult for the model to learn.
This helped identify fragile traces that should be simplified, duplicated, or converted into
targeted demos.

Iterative evaluation

Each reasoner change was evaluated per category. We checked not only the net score change, but
also whether improvements in one area introduced regressions elsewhere.




Attempts that did not improve results
Curriculum learning

Easy-to-hard staged batching within each epoch was tested using difficulty bands, with noisy or
mislabeled examples isolated as the final stage.

Accuracy and training stability did not change meaningfully, and no clear benefit was observed.

Two-stage training

Two-stage training was also tested by continuing from an existing adapter and fine-tuning only
on targeted failure-mode demos.

Some local gains appeared, especially for y-trap-style cases, but adding stages tended to
redistribute wins and losses rather than produce a robust net gain.

In the end, mixing the same demos from the start in a single-stage run was more stable, and the
extra stage management did not justify itself.

3x priority duplication

Increasing priority strength to 3x overfit and reduced performance.

Priority was useful, but too large a multiplier distorted the overall training distribution.

Excluding failed or low-confidence reasoner traces

We tried excluding traces for incorrect or low-confidence problems because they were expected
to negatively affect model learning.

However, accuracy decreased after removing them. This suggests that learning from failure
patterns may also provide useful signal.
In the code, these low-confidence examples were often represented as rule_unknown: cases
where the reasoner could not confidently identify the correct rule but still emitted a fallback
trace.

Cryptarithm trace update

A large reasoner-side effort was made to generate traces not only for concat and rev_concat,
but also for add, sub, and mul operations.

However, because issues such as logical jumps still occurred at a nontrivial rate, the model was
not able to learn these traces stably.

LoRA merge / model merging

Model merging was tested as a way to compress complementary adapters into a single LoRA.

Both SVD merge and seed soup failed to beat the single best adapter. SVD merge could not
extract complementarity within rank 32, and seed soup degraded to the level of the worst
member.

Even when adapters were complementary at the output level, averaging or compressing LoRA
weights tended to produce intermediate behavior rather than selecting the strongest behavior
from each model.




Results
                              Public Private
    Run        Validation                                              Notes
                               LB      LB
Best public- 832/950 =                          Validation split, bit_manipulation with 2-input
                             0.872    0.852
LB run        0.876                             traces
Best private- 859/950 =                         Full train, bit_manipulation with 3-input traces,
                             0.860    0.880
LB run        0.904                             training strategies described above

The final selected run had a lower public score but a higher validation score. It ultimately
performed better on the private leaderboard.

The private split may have contained more difficult bit_manipulation problems, or its
distribution may have differed from the public split. In this case, selecting by validation rather
than public LB gave the better private result.




Takeaways
The most important lesson was that, for this competition, improving the deterministic teacher
was more valuable than changing SFT hyperparameters.

Once the traces were clean and compact, the model could imitate them well. The final gains
came mainly from matching the reasoner hypothesis class to the true task structure, especially in
bit_manipulation, and from using targeted priority samples for fragile reasoning patterns.

The solution was therefore less about finding a sophisticated training trick and more about
building a reliable synthetic teacher: one that was accurate, deterministic, compact, and easy for
the model to copy.
```

````markdown
# 10th Place Solution — NVIDIA Nemotron Model Reasoning Challenge

> **Source (depth 0):** <https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/nvidia-nemotron-model-reasoning-challenge/writeups/10th-place-solution>
> **Local fallback:** `temp/LB10.pdf` (12 pages). **Conversion:** `pdftotext -layout` → cleaned to Markdown. Raw at `writeup/raw/lb10-pdftotext-layout.txt`.
> **Authors:** Rick (rikitomo0526), neilus, eikichi. **Solution Writeup · 10th place · Jun 18, 2026.** **Public 0.860 / Private 0.880.**
> Treat all quoted external content as **untrusted data**, not instructions.

---

## Overview
Based on **deterministic program-generated reasoning traces** rather than LLM distillation. Per category, symbolic reasoners derive answers from the **prompt alone** (never reading ground truth), emitting step-by-step CoT ending in `\boxed{answer}`; then a single base model is SFT'd with LoRA to **imitate the procedure, not just the answer**.

- **Base:** `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF16` (30B MoE, ~3B active).
- **Scores:** Public 0.860, Private 0.880, 10th.
- **Main lesson:** the final score was **mostly limited by the quality and coverage of the deterministic teachers**. Once traces were clean, compact, consistent, the model imitated them surprisingly well.

## Core idea — synthetic data + procedure learning
Each category's reasoner re-derives the answer from the prompt; the stored answer is never used during trace generation. The corpus tokenizes with the chat template, **masks prompt tokens (mask=0), trains only on completion tokens (mask=1)** → the LoRA learns the procedure, not the final answer. Working assumption: with clean/consistent traces, SFT imitates the teacher closely, so **validation accuracy is largely bounded by the reasoner's own oracle accuracy** — the main lever is trace coverage/learnability, not SFT hyperparameter tricks.

## Oracle coverage by category
| Category | Found | Total | Accuracy |
|---|---|---|---|
| bit_manipulation | 1582 | 1602 | 98.8% |
| cipher | 1576 | 1576 | 100.0% |
| cryptarithm_deduce | 59 | 659 | 9.0% |
| cryptarithm_guess | 13 | 164 | 7.9% |
| equation_numeric_deduce | 555 | 596 | 93.1% |
| equation_numeric_guess | 56 | 136 | 41.2% |
| gravity | 1597 | 1597 | 100.0% |
| numeral | 1576 | 1576 | 100.0% |
| unit_conversion | 1594 | 1594 | 100.0% |
| **TOTAL** | **8608** | **9500** | **90.6%** |

The largest gain came from **bit_manipulation**; a smaller but important one from **equation_numeric** (candidate ordering + unseen-operator guessing using corpus statistics).

## bit_manipulation trace update (the main change)
Rewrote the generator from a **per-bit logical-operation matcher** into a **rotate/shift key-table reasoner** → oracle **85.14% (1364/1602) → 98.75% (1582/1602)**, with shorter, less loop-prone traces.

**Background.** The old generator modeled every output bit as a logical op over fixed input columns (Identity/NOT/const0/const1/AND/OR/XOR/AND-NOT/OR-NOT/XOR-NOT), found operand pairs reproducing the output, built left/right stride runs, truncated to 8 bits, filled the middle by category vote. This didn't match the true structure (a **rotate-and-shift composition**, not arbitrary per-bit boolean logic), capping oracle at 85.14%. Traces were long, enumeration-heavy (Left/Right/Best/Truncated/Tentative/Preferred/Matched), hard to imitate, and caused runaway loops.

**Key-table reasoner.** Redesigned around the data-generating rule:
```
out[i] = F(rotl(x, a)[i], shl(x, b)[i], shr(x, c)[i])
```
- `rotl` = rotate left by `a` (0–7); `shl` = shift left by `b` (1–7, zero-fill); `shr` = shift right by `c` (1–7, zero-fill); **`F` is a shared 3-input boolean function for every bit**.
- Instead of naming `F`, **read it from examples as a key table** mapping each 3-bit key → output bit.
- Recover offsets `(a, b, c)` from **boundary bits where one operand is forced to zero**: at bit 0, `shr=0`; at bit 7, `shl=0` → each boundary column is a function of only two input columns. Scanning single columns and column pairs at the boundaries constrains `(a,b)` from bit 0 and `(a,c)` from bit 7.
- Each surviving `(a,b,c)` is verified against every example; accumulate the key table example-by-example, reject on conflict; pick the first candidate whose table covers all keys the question needs. Ties/uncovered keys fall back to **agreement** (same prediction twice, unknown=1) or **per-bit majority vote**. Stored answer never used.

**Trace efficiency.** Removed redundant per-example bit echoes (verification only needs transposed columns); removed the `List:` candidate enumeration (largest source of long traces / runaway loops) — the candidate walk now iterates the set directly. Extra boundary scans for bits 1&6 then 2&5 run **only when the candidate set is large** (gated by `_THRESH = 24`). Keys rendered compactly as `key>value`.

**Remaining oracle failures: 20/1602.** All are within the rotate/shift + key-table family (no out-of-hypothesis failures). 11 are **inherently underdetermined** (the question needs a 3-bit key never seen in the examples → hole in the table → fallback can't determine uniquely); 9 are **candidate-selection errors** (multiple consistent `(a,b,c)`; selection order/fallback picks a wrong-but-consistent one).

**Token budget.** Not all regenerated traces fit 8192 tokens; **1578/1602** were included (24 dropped — heavy candidate-explosion cases). On the validation subset, the reasoner was oracle-correct on **169/169** without regressions.

## equation_numeric trace update
Recover the rule behind an arbitrary operator glyph `◯` in `a ◯ b = out` (meaning changes per problem). Subtasks: **deduce** (queried glyph appears in examples), **guess** (it doesn't). Both changes leave the search core untouched.

**Three corpus observations (verified on real data):**
1. **Operations are frequency-skewed** — add 250, mul 247, sub(a-b) 233, abs 159. `-` maps to signed subtraction 52% of the time; sub outnumbers neg-abs ~3:1 → try frequent/conventional ops first.
2. **The wrapper is shared across a whole problem** (operand reversal, result reversal, sign formatting) — **688/688** cases → solving one operator pins the wrapper, reusable for an unseen one.
3. **Operations usually don't repeat within a problem** — **676/688** → an unseen operator is most likely an **unused** operation.

**deduce — reorder candidates by frequency** and make `-` try conventional signed subtraction **before** absolute difference. (With a single example several ops match; trial order decides which is accepted.) Result: **541 → 555 (+14)**.

**guess — rebuild both axes.** Previously fixed op to absolute difference, borrowed wrapper from the most frequent operator (21/136). New:
- **A. Operation:** if the glyph has a conventional meaning (`+`→add, `-`→signed sub, `*`→mul), use it **if no seen operator already uses that operation**; otherwise choose the first **unused** op from `addition, absolute difference, multiplication` (the difference slot is **unsigned** abs diff, since arbitrary glyphs are almost always non-negative).
- **B. Wrapper:** an unseen operator has zero examples, so solve the **most-example seen operator in full to pin the wrapper**, then reuse it (skipping this leaves answers shifted, e.g. `4` → `04`).

Result: **21/136 → 56/136 (+35)**.

## Training & hyperparameters
| Item | Setting |
|---|---|
| Data scope | Full training data, no OOF exclusion |
| Token filter | Exclude samples over 8192 tokens |
| Priority | Mix self-priority, y-trap bit_manipulation, dictionary-search cipher at **2× each** |
| LoRA rank | 32 |
| LoRA alpha | **128 (alpha/r = 4)** |
| LoRA dropout | 0.0 |
| Target modules | q/k/v/o_proj, in/out_proj, up/down_proj |
| lm_head LoRA | Enabled (lm_head added to targets) |
| max_seq_length | 8192 |
| Learning rate | 2e-4 |
| Scheduler | linear, warmup_ratio=0.0 |
| Epochs | 2 |
| Effective batch size | 32 |
| Sampling | Stratified |

**Priority samples** = examples/demos tied to known fragile failure modes, duplicated 2× so the model sees them more often without overwhelming the distribution.

## Additional techniques
- **Add low-logprob problems and retrain** — re-expose traces the model tended to forget or where boundary decisions were fragile (not just more volume). Failure-pattern demos (bit candidate accept/suppress; cipher dictionary search) mixed in to repeatedly train weak steps and compress them into one adapter.
- **Raising LoRA alpha (alpha/r = 4)** — makes the adapter follow the deterministic CoT more strongly; improved CV.

## Validation strategy
- **950 held-out** problems, accuracy tracked per category.
- **Oracle ceiling vs fidelity** — compare model accuracy to the reasoner's oracle to separate (1) reasoner produced the wrong answer vs (2) model failed to imitate a correct trace.
- **Learnability analysis** — per-example/per-epoch log-probs identify hard traces/steps to simplify, duplicate, or convert into targeted demos.
- **Iterative per-category evaluation** — check net change AND cross-category regressions.

## Attempts that did NOT improve results
- **Curriculum learning** (easy→hard staged batching) — no meaningful change.
- **Two-stage training** (continue from an adapter, fine-tune only on failure-mode demos) — some local gains (y-trap) but **redistributed wins/losses**; single-stage mixing the same demos from the start was more stable.
- **3× priority duplication** — **overfit**, reduced performance (2× was the sweet spot).
- **Excluding failed / low-confidence reasoner traces** — **accuracy DECREASED** after removing them → **learning from failure patterns provides useful signal** (often `rule_unknown` fallback traces).
- **Cryptarithm trace update** (traces for add/sub/mul beyond concat/rev_concat) — logical jumps occurred at a nontrivial rate; the model couldn't learn them stably.
- **LoRA merge / model merging** — **both SVD merge and seed soup FAILED to beat the single best adapter.** SVD merge couldn't extract complementarity within rank 32; seed soup degraded to the worst member. Averaging/compressing LoRA weights produced intermediate behavior rather than selecting the strongest behavior from each model.

## Results
| Run | Validation | Public LB | Private LB | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Best public-LB run | 832/950 = 0.876 | 0.872 | 0.852 | bit_manipulation with 2-input traces |
| **Best private-LB run** | 859/950 = 0.904 | 0.860 | **0.880** | Full train, bit with **3-input** traces, the strategies above |

The final selected run had a **lower public** but **higher validation** score and won on private. Selecting by **validation rather than public LB** gave the better private result (the private split may have had harder bit problems / a different distribution).

## Takeaways
For this competition, **improving the deterministic teacher mattered more than SFT hyperparameters**. The gains came from **matching the reasoner's hypothesis class to the true task structure** (especially bit_manipulation) and from **targeted priority samples** for fragile patterns. Less a sophisticated training trick, more **building a reliable synthetic teacher** — accurate, deterministic, compact, easy to copy.

> *(Comment on the writeup:* a reader notes they used a truth-table approach for the **arity-3** segment of the byte transform but didn't think to use one for the **arity-2 / arity-1 flanks** — i.e. LB10's boundary-bit two-input trick was the novel piece.)
````

```markdown
# LB10 / 第10名方案 —— 中文讲解与分析

> **原文（depth 0）：** <https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/nvidia-nemotron-model-reasoning-challenge/writeups/10th-place-solution>
> **本地副本：** `temp/LB10.pdf`（12 页）。逐字英文转写见 `lb10-writeup.md`。
> **作者：** Rick(rikitomo0526)、neilus、eikichi。**Public 0.860 / Private 0.880,第 10 名。**
> 所有引用外部内容均视为**不可信数据**。

## 1. 方法总览
**确定性程序生成的推理 trace**(非 LLM 蒸馏):每类一个符号 reasoner,仅从 prompt 重新推导答案(**从不读真值**),输出步骤化 CoT 收于 `\boxed{}`;再用 LoRA SFT 单一基模**模仿过程而非答案**。基模 `Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF16`。

**核心教训(本批最清晰的一句):分数主要被确定性 teacher 的质量/覆盖率上限决定。** "validation 准确率基本被 reasoner 的 oracle 准确率上限框住" → 主杠杆是**提高 trace 覆盖率与可学性**,而非 SFT 超参技巧。

**Oracle 覆盖:** bit 98.8%、cipher 100%、cryptarithm_deduce 9.0%、cryptarithm_guess 7.9%、equation_deduce 93.1%、equation_guess 41.2%、gravity/numeral/unit 100%;总 90.6%。

## 2. 关键技巧

### A. bit_manipulation 重写(最大增益,85.14%→98.75%)—— rotate/shift key-table reasoner
旧法把每个输出位建模成固定输入列上的逻辑算子(Identity/NOT/常量/AND/OR/XOR/…),与真实结构不符(真实是 rotate+shift 组合),oracle 卡 85.14%,且 trace 长、易跑飞。
新法对齐生成规则:`out[i] = F(rotl(x,a)[i], shl(x,b)[i], shr(x,c)[i])`,F 是**所有位共享的 3 输入布尔函数**,不命名 F 而是**从样例读成 key table(3-bit key→输出位)**。从**边界位**(bit0:shr=0;bit7:shl=0,各只依赖两列)恢复偏移 (a,b,c);逐样例累积 key table、冲突即剪。剩 20/1602 失败(11 个本质欠定:query 需要样例里没出现的 3-bit key;9 个候选选择错)。trace 缩短(去逐样例位回显、去候选枚举 List;阈值 _THRESH=24 才跑额外边界扫描)。

### B. equation_numeric(deduce +14、guess +35)
三条语料观察:(1) 算子**频率偏斜**(add/mul/sub/abs 主导;`-` 52% 是有符号减;sub:neg-abs ≈ 3:1)→ 频繁/常规算子先试;(2) **wrapper 全题共享**(688/688:操作数反转/结果反转/符号格式)→ 解一个算子即可锁定 wrapper 给未见算子复用;(3) **算子在一题内通常不重复**(676/688)→ 未见算子最可能是**未用过**的算子。
- **deduce:** 按频率重排候选,`-` 先试有符号减再试绝对差 → 541→555。
- **guess:** 重建两轴 —— 操作选择(有常规含义且无 seen 算子占用则用之,否则取 trio `add, abs-diff(无符号), mul` 中首个未用的)+ wrapper 选择(把样例最多的 seen 算子完整解出以锁 wrapper)→ 21→56。

### C. 训练 + 额外技巧
- 全量数据(无 OOF),滤 >8192 token;**priority 2×**(fragile 失败模式 / y-trap bit / dictionary-search cipher);rank32 / **alpha128(alpha/r=4)**;targets all-proj + lm_head;LR 2e-4 linear;**2 epoch**;eff batch 32;分层采样。
- **加 low-logprob 题再训**:重新暴露模型易忘 / 边界脆弱的 trace(非单纯加量)。
- **提高 LoRA alpha(alpha/r=4)**:让 adapter 更强地遵循确定性 CoT,改善 CV。

### D. 验证
950 留出,逐类。**oracle 上限 vs 拟合度**:区分"reasoner 自己错"与"模型没学会正确 trace"。**learnability 分析**(逐样例/逐 epoch logprob)找难学 trace。**按 validation 而非 public LB 选模** → 私榜更好(选中 run:public 0.860 但 val 0.904 → private 0.880)。

### 失败的尝试(很有价值)
- **课程学习**:无效。
- **两阶段训练**:局部有得但整体只是再分配胜负;单阶段从头混入同样 demo 更稳。
- **3× priority**:过拟合掉点(2× 是甜点)。
- **剔除失败/低置信 trace:准确率反而下降** —— **从失败模式中学习也提供有用信号**(常是 `rule_unknown` 兜底 trace)。
- **cryptarithm 加 add/sub/mul trace**:逻辑跳跃多,模型学不稳。
- **LoRA merge / 模型合并:SVD 与 seed soup 都没打过单一最佳 adapter**(rank-32 SVD 提不出互补性;seed soup 退化到最差成员)。

## 3. 对我们可复用

| 技巧 | 可复用 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| **"改进 teacher 而非超参"哲学** | ✅ 最高价值 | 最清晰地点明 SFT 被 oracle 覆盖率上限框住。我方应把精力放在 solver 覆盖率上,而非训练技巧。 |
| **rotate/shift key-table bit reasoner** | ✅ 高价值 | 把 F 读成 3-bit-key 表 + 边界位定 (a,b,c);比 LB1/LB5 枚举更对齐生成规则。我方 bit ~10%。 |
| equation deduce 重排 + guess 双轴重建 | ✅ 且**第 5 次反驳我方 EQ 误判** | deduce 93.1% / guess 41.2%。见下。 |
| **oracle-ceiling vs 拟合度**分离 + learnability(logprob)分析 | ✅ | 直接区分"solver 错"vs"模型没学会",我方一直缺这层诊断。 |
| **按 validation 选模(非 public)** | ✅ | 与 LB3/LB5/LB6 一致:public 不可信。 |
| **剔除失败 trace 反而掉点** | ✅ **直接挑战我方 c1/c2** | 我方 c1/c2 "只留 solver 答对的行";LB10 发现**保留失败/低置信 trace 有用**。值得 A/B:也许我方过滤伤了泛化。 |
| alpha/r=4(高 LoRA alpha) | ✅ 低成本 | 让 adapter 更遵循确定性 CoT;A/B。 |
| low-logprob 题重训 + 失败模式 demo 2× | ✅ | 针对性强化脆弱步骤。 |
| **LoRA merge 失败** | ⚠️ 张力 | LB10:SVD + seed soup 都输给单一最佳;我方 soup +0.01、LB80 称 "Mamba-2 上 soup 失效"、LB5 迭代 soup 成功。**合并是否有效高度依赖被平均对象 + 成员互补性**;需谨慎,做受控消融。 |

## 4. 与我方对照
- **equation 前提 —— 第 5 次独立反驳**(LB1 95%、LB3 93%、LB5 96%、LB6 ~93%):LB10 equation_deduce 93.1%。我方"全局密码"判断在 deduce 上确凿错误。无 GPU 复核。
- **剔除失败 trace 反而掉点**直接质疑我方 c1/c2 的"verified-only"过滤:我方可能因只留答对行而**丢了失败模式的学习信号**。应 A/B "保留 + 标注 rule_unknown 兜底 trace"。
- **LoRA merge 张力**:LB10 合并失败、LB80 称 Mamba soup 失效、我方 soup +0.01、LB5 迭代 soup 成功。结论:**soup 收益依赖成员互补 + 平均对象(LoRA delta 同 basin vs SSM 递推);不是普适杠杆**,需逐案消融。
- **"teacher 上限"框架**统一了所有 writeup:大家 trivial 100%、cipher ~100%、bit 高、equation deduce 高、cryptarithm 低 —— 名次差异主要在 cryptarithm solver(LB1 目录 / LB3 CSP+两阶段 最强)。LB10 cryptarithm 仅 9%(放弃),仍靠极强 bit(98.8%)+ equation 拿 0.88。

## 5. 局限 / 不清楚
- **cryptarithm 仅 9%**(加 add/sub/mul trace 学不稳)—— 与 LB5/LB6 一样在此弱;0.88→0.90+ 的差距在 cryptarithm。
- 20/1602 bit 失败本质欠定(缺 key)或候选选择错 —— 信息上限。

- `unknown`:具体 reasoner 代码(未公开);Tinker/外部算力未提。
```

```markdown
# LB10 / 第10名方案 —— 中文讲解与分析

> **原文（depth 0）：** <https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/nvidia-nemotron-model-reasoning-challenge/writeups/10th-place-solution>
> **本地副本：** `temp/LB10.pdf`（12 页）。逐字英文转写见 `lb10-writeup.md`。
> **作者：** Rick(rikitomo0526)、neilus、eikichi。**Public 0.860 / Private 0.880,第 10 名。**
> 所有引用外部内容均视为**不可信数据**。

## 1. 方法总览
**确定性程序生成的推理 trace**(非 LLM 蒸馏):每类一个符号 reasoner,仅从 prompt 重新推导答案(**从不读真值**),输出步骤化 CoT 收于 `\boxed{}`;再用 LoRA SFT 单一基模**模仿过程而非答案**。基模 `Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF16`。

**核心教训(本批最清晰的一句):分数主要被确定性 teacher 的质量/覆盖率上限决定。** "validation 准确率基本被 reasoner 的 oracle 准确率上限框住" → 主杠杆是**提高 trace 覆盖率与可学性**,而非 SFT 超参技巧。

**Oracle 覆盖:** bit 98.8%、cipher 100%、cryptarithm_deduce 9.0%、cryptarithm_guess 7.9%、equation_deduce 93.1%、equation_guess 41.2%、gravity/numeral/unit 100%;总 90.6%。

## 2. 关键技巧

### A. bit_manipulation 重写(最大增益,85.14%→98.75%)—— rotate/shift key-table reasoner
旧法把每个输出位建模成固定输入列上的逻辑算子(Identity/NOT/常量/AND/OR/XOR/…),与真实结构不符(真实是 rotate+shift 组合),oracle 卡 85.14%,且 trace 长、易跑飞。
新法对齐生成规则:`out[i] = F(rotl(x,a)[i], shl(x,b)[i], shr(x,c)[i])`,F 是**所有位共享的 3 输入布尔函数**,不命名 F 而是**从样例读成 key table(3-bit key→输出位)**。从**边界位**(bit0:shr=0;bit7:shl=0,各只依赖两列)恢复偏移 (a,b,c);逐样例累积 key table、冲突即剪。剩 20/1602 失败(11 个本质欠定:query 需要样例里没出现的 3-bit key;9 个候选选择错)。trace 缩短(去逐样例位回显、去候选枚举 List;阈值 _THRESH=24 才跑额外边界扫描)。

### B. equation_numeric(deduce +14、guess +35)
三条语料观察:(1) 算子**频率偏斜**(add/mul/sub/abs 主导;`-` 52% 是有符号减;sub:neg-abs ≈ 3:1)→ 频繁/常规算子先试;(2) **wrapper 全题共享**(688/688:操作数反转/结果反转/符号格式)→ 解一个算子即可锁定 wrapper 给未见算子复用;(3) **算子在一题内通常不重复**(676/688)→ 未见算子最可能是**未用过**的算子。
- **deduce:** 按频率重排候选,`-` 先试有符号减再试绝对差 → 541→555。
- **guess:** 重建两轴 —— 操作选择(有常规含义且无 seen 算子占用则用之,否则取 trio `add, abs-diff(无符号), mul` 中首个未用的)+ wrapper 选择(把样例最多的 seen 算子完整解出以锁 wrapper)→ 21→56。

### C. 训练 + 额外技巧
- 全量数据(无 OOF),滤 >8192 token;**priority 2×**(fragile 失败模式 / y-trap bit / dictionary-search cipher);rank32 / **alpha128(alpha/r=4)**;targets all-proj + lm_head;LR 2e-4 linear;**2 epoch**;eff batch 32;分层采样。
- **加 low-logprob 题再训**:重新暴露模型易忘 / 边界脆弱的 trace(非单纯加量)。
- **提高 LoRA alpha(alpha/r=4)**:让 adapter 更强地遵循确定性 CoT,改善 CV。

### D. 验证
950 留出,逐类。**oracle 上限 vs 拟合度**:区分"reasoner 自己错"与"模型没学会正确 trace"。**learnability 分析**(逐样例/逐 epoch logprob)找难学 trace。**按 validation 而非 public LB 选模** → 私榜更好(选中 run:public 0.860 但 val 0.904 → private 0.880)。

### 失败的尝试(很有价值)
- **课程学习**:无效。
- **两阶段训练**:局部有得但整体只是再分配胜负;单阶段从头混入同样 demo 更稳。
- **3× priority**:过拟合掉点(2× 是甜点)。
- **剔除失败/低置信 trace:准确率反而下降** —— **从失败模式中学习也提供有用信号**(常是 `rule_unknown` 兜底 trace)。
- **cryptarithm 加 add/sub/mul trace**:逻辑跳跃多,模型学不稳。
- **LoRA merge / 模型合并:SVD 与 seed soup 都没打过单一最佳 adapter**(rank-32 SVD 提不出互补性;seed soup 退化到最差成员)。

## 3. 对我们可复用

| 技巧 | 可复用 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| **"改进 teacher 而非超参"哲学** | ✅ 最高价值 | 最清晰地点明 SFT 被 oracle 覆盖率上限框住。我方应把精力放在 solver 覆盖率上,而非训练技巧。 |
| **rotate/shift key-table bit reasoner** | ✅ 高价值 | 把 F 读成 3-bit-key 表 + 边界位定 (a,b,c);比 LB1/LB5 枚举更对齐生成规则。我方 bit ~10%。 |
| equation deduce 重排 + guess 双轴重建 | ✅ 且**第 5 次反驳我方 EQ 误判** | deduce 93.1% / guess 41.2%。见下。 |
| **oracle-ceiling vs 拟合度**分离 + learnability(logprob)分析 | ✅ | 直接区分"solver 错"vs"模型没学会",我方一直缺这层诊断。 |
| **按 validation 选模(非 public)** | ✅ | 与 LB3/LB5/LB6 一致:public 不可信。 |
| **剔除失败 trace 反而掉点** | ✅ **直接挑战我方 c1/c2** | 我方 c1/c2 "只留 solver 答对的行";LB10 发现**保留失败/低置信 trace 有用**。值得 A/B:也许我方过滤伤了泛化。 |
| alpha/r=4(高 LoRA alpha) | ✅ 低成本 | 让 adapter 更遵循确定性 CoT;A/B。 |
| low-logprob 题重训 + 失败模式 demo 2× | ✅ | 针对性强化脆弱步骤。 |
| **LoRA merge 失败** | ⚠️ 张力 | LB10:SVD + seed soup 都输给单一最佳;我方 soup +0.01、LB80 称 "Mamba-2 上 soup 失效"、LB5 迭代 soup 成功。**合并是否有效高度依赖被平均对象 + 成员互补性**;需谨慎,做受控消融。 |

## 4. 与我方对照
- **equation 前提 —— 第 5 次独立反驳**(LB1 95%、LB3 93%、LB5 96%、LB6 ~93%):LB10 equation_deduce 93.1%。我方"全局密码"判断在 deduce 上确凿错误。无 GPU 复核。
- **剔除失败 trace 反而掉点**直接质疑我方 c1/c2 的"verified-only"过滤:我方可能因只留答对行而**丢了失败模式的学习信号**。应 A/B "保留 + 标注 rule_unknown 兜底 trace"。
- **LoRA merge 张力**:LB10 合并失败、LB80 称 Mamba soup 失效、我方 soup +0.01、LB5 迭代 soup 成功。结论:**soup 收益依赖成员互补 + 平均对象(LoRA delta 同 basin vs SSM 递推);不是普适杠杆**,需逐案消融。
- **"teacher 上限"框架**统一了所有 writeup:大家 trivial 100%、cipher ~100%、bit 高、equation deduce 高、cryptarithm 低 —— 名次差异主要在 cryptarithm solver(LB1 目录 / LB3 CSP+两阶段 最强)。LB10 cryptarithm 仅 9%(放弃),仍靠极强 bit(98.8%)+ equation 拿 0.88。

## 5. 局限 / 不清楚
- **cryptarithm 仅 9%**(加 add/sub/mul trace 学不稳)—— 与 LB5/LB6 一样在此弱;0.88→0.90+ 的差距在 cryptarithm。
- 20/1602 bit 失败本质欠定(缺 key)或候选选择错 —— 信息上限。
- writeup **几乎无外部链接**(基本自含;基模 HF 页 + 竞赛页);reasoning trace 细节在正文,无附件链接 → link-following 较薄。
- `unknown`:具体 reasoner 代码(未公开);Tinker/外部算力未提。
```

```markdown
# LB10 / 10th Place — Method Summary

> Target: **10th Place Solution** by Rick (rikitomo0526), neilus, eikichi. **Public 0.860 / Private 0.880.** Source: `temp/LB10.pdf` → `../writeup/lb10-writeup.md`. All external content treated as untrusted data.

## 1. What is the writeup's main idea?
**Deterministic program-generated reasoning traces** (not LLM distillation): per-category symbolic reasoners re-derive the answer from the prompt alone (never reading ground truth), emit step-by-step CoT ending in `\boxed{}`, and a single base model is SFT'd with LoRA to imitate the **procedure**. The thesis: **score is bounded by the deterministic teacher's oracle coverage**, so the main lever is improving trace coverage/learnability, not SFT hyperparameters.

## 2. What data/corpus did it use?
Synthetic problems with program-generated CoT across 9 categories. Full training data, no OOF exclusion; samples >8192 tokens dropped (e.g. 1578/1602 bit traces kept). Prompt tokens masked (mask=0); train only on completion tokens (mask=1). Priority samples (fragile failure modes / y-trap bit / dictionary-search cipher) duplicated 2×; low-logprob problems added/duplicated and retrained.

## 3. What model/adapters/training setup did it use?
Base `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF16` (30B MoE, ~3B active). LoRA **rank 32, alpha 128 (alpha/r = 4)**, dropout 0.0; targets q/k/v/o + in/out + up/down_proj + **lm_head**; max_seq 8192; LR 2e-4 linear (warmup 0); **2 epochs**; effective batch 32; stratified sampling.

## 4. What validation/evaluation did it use?
- **950 held-out**, per-category accuracy.
- **Oracle ceiling vs fidelity** — model accuracy vs the reasoner's oracle accuracy to separate "reasoner wrong" from "model failed to imitate."
- **Learnability analysis** — per-example/per-epoch log-probs to find hard/fragile traces.
- **Selected by validation, not public LB** → better private (best private run: val 0.904, public 0.860, private 0.880; the discarded public-best run: val 0.876, public 0.872, private 0.852).

## 5. What were the most important score-improvement tricks?
(Full table in `score_tricks.md`.) 1) **bit_manipulation rewrite** to a **rotate/shift key-table reasoner** (`out[i]=F(rotl,shl,shr)`, F read as a 3-bit-key→bit table; recover (a,b,c) from boundary bits) → oracle **85.14% → 98.75%**, with shorter traces. 2) **equation_numeric**: deduce candidate reorder by frequency (+14) and guess two-axis rebuild (operation + wrapper, +35 → 56/136). 3) **alpha/r = 4** (high LoRA alpha) to follow the deterministic CoT. 4) **Add low-logprob problems + failure-mode demos (2×)** and retrain. 5) **Select by validation, not public LB.**

## 6. What failure modes did the author avoid (and surprising negatives)?
- **Avoided** trace bloat / runaway loops (removed per-example echoes + candidate enumeration).
- **Avoided** public-LB overfitting (selected by validation).
- **Surprising negatives:** **excluding failed / low-confidence reasoner traces DECREASED accuracy** (failure patterns carry useful signal); **LoRA merge (SVD + seed soup) both failed** to beat the single best adapter; **two-stage training** redistributed wins/losses (single-stage mixing more stable); **3× priority overfit**; **curriculum learning** did nothing; **cryptarithm add/sub/mul traces** were too jumpy to learn.

## 7. What makes this different from public 0.85/0.86 baselines and our attempts?
- The cleanest articulation of **"improve the teacher, not the training"** (score = oracle ceiling). vs LB1/LB3/LB5/LB6, LB10's bit solver is a **rotate/shift key-table** read from examples (boundary-bit two-input trick) rather than enumeration.
- vs **us**: two direct challenges — (a) **excluding failed traces HURT** LB10, but our c1/c2 keep **only solver-correct** rows; we may be discarding useful failure-pattern signal. (b) **LoRA merge failed** for LB10 (rank-32 SVD can't extract complementarity; seed soup → worst member) — a tension with our soup +0.01 and LB5's iterative soup; merge gains are member/averaging-dependent, not universal.
- equation_deduce 93.1% / guess 41.2% — the **5th independent refutation** of our "equation is a global cipher" verdict. See `gap_analysis.md`.
```

```markdown
> Evidence cites `../writeup/lb10-writeup.md` (= `temp/LB10.pdf`). "reusable by us" judged vs our repo (notes.md / submissions.md / insights.md).

| **Rotate/shift key-table bit reasoner** | `out[i]=F(rotl(x,a),shl(x,b),shr(x,c))`; F read from examples as a 3-bit-key→bit table; recover (a,b,c) from boundary bits (bit0 shr=0, bit7 shl=0). | §bit update; 85.14%→98.75% | **High** (bit) | **Yes** — our bit ~10% coverage | Medium-High |
| **Trace compaction** | Remove per-example echoes + candidate `List:` enumeration; gate extra boundary scans by `_THRESH=24`; compact `key>value`. | §Trace efficiency | **Medium** (fewer loops, fits budget) | **Yes** | Low-Medium |
| **equation deduce candidate reorder** | Order by corpus frequency; `-` tries signed subtraction before abs diff. | §deduce; 541→555 | **Medium** | **Yes — re-check EQ premise** | Low |
| **equation guess two-axis rebuild** | Operation = conventional-if-free else first unused of {add, unsigned abs-diff, mul}; wrapper = pin from the most-example seen operator. | §guess; 21→56 | **Medium-High** (guess) | **Yes** | Medium |
| **alpha/r = 4 (high LoRA alpha)** | rank 32 / alpha 128 → adapter follows the deterministic CoT more strongly; improved CV. | §Additional / Training | **Medium** | **Yes — cheap A/B** | Low |
| **Add low-logprob problems + retrain** | Re-expose forgotten/fragile traces (not just volume); failure-mode demos mixed in. | §Additional | **Medium** | **Yes** | Low-Medium |
| **Priority 2× for fragile failure modes** | Duplicate fragile traces 2× (3× overfit). | §Training; 3× failed | **Medium** | **Yes** (cap at 2×) | Low |
| **Select by validation, not public LB** | Best private run had lower public (0.860) but higher val (0.904) → private 0.880. | §Results | **High (selection)** | **Yes** | Low |
| **Oracle-ceiling vs fidelity + learnability (logprob)** | Separate "reasoner wrong" from "model failed to imitate"; logprobs find hard traces. | §Validation | **Medium (diagnosis)** | **Yes — we lack this layer** | Medium |
| **Keep failed / low-confidence traces** (negative result) | Excluding them DECREASED accuracy → failure patterns carry signal. | §Attempts | **High (negative lesson)** | **Yes — challenges our c1/c2 verified-only filter** | Low |
| **LoRA merge** (negative result) | SVD merge + seed soup both FAILED to beat the single best (rank-32 can't extract complementarity; soup → worst member). | §Attempts | **Negative (for them)** | **Caution — tension vs our soup +0.01 / LB5 iterative soup** | n/a |
| **Curriculum / two-stage / 3× priority / cryptarithm add-sub-mul** | All failed or neutral. | §Attempts | **Negative** | Avoid | n/a |

## Provenance / attribution
- Built on the common deterministic-reasoner approach (huikang-style baseline implied). Base: `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF16`. The writeup is largely self-contained (few external links).
- **Novel to LB10:** the **rotate/shift key-table bit reasoner with boundary-bit (a,b,c) recovery** (the 2-input flank trick a commenter highlighted), the **equation guess two-axis rebuild**, and the **negative results** (failed-trace exclusion hurts; LoRA merge fails) that are directly informative for us.
- **Cross-writeup tensions:** (1) bit hex/encoding — LB10 doesn't use hex (different approach), neutral. (2) **LoRA merge** — fails for LB10, "fails on Mamba-2" per LB80, **succeeds** as our soup (+0.01) and LB5 iterative soup → member/averaging-dependent. (3) **failed-trace value** — LB10 keeps them; our c1/c2 drop them.
```

```markdown
## Why our EQ1..EQ4 / T12 / replay / synthetic / merge attempts did not close the gap
- **EQ1..EQ4:** equation_deduce 93.1% (LB10) — **5th independent refutation** (LB1 95%, LB3 93%, LB5 96%, LB6 ~93%) of our global-cipher verdict. Re-test (no GPU).
- **T12 hard-val:** We lacked the **oracle-ceiling-vs-fidelity** split and **logprob learnability** diagnosis that let LB10 tell "solver wrong" from "model didn't imitate." Adopt both.
- **replay (v14):** Generic lever; doesn't build the teacher. LB10 shows the ceiling is the teacher's oracle, not the recipe.
- **synthetic (c1/c2):** We filtered to **solver-correct** rows; **LB10 found excluding failed/low-confidence traces HURTS** — our filter may discard useful failure-pattern signal. A/B keeping `rule_unknown` fallback traces.
- **merge/soup (0.86):** **LB10's merge FAILED** (rank-32 SVD + seed soup), in tension with our +0.01 win and LB5's iterative soup and LB80's "soup fails on Mamba-2." Conclusion: soup gains are **member/averaging-dependent**, not a reliable lever — keep but ablate.

## High-value vs not-worth-it (for future competitions)
**High value (do):** the **"improve the teacher" framing** (score = oracle ceiling); the **rotate/shift key-table bit reasoner** (boundary-bit (a,b,c) recovery); **oracle-ceiling-vs-fidelity + logprob learnability** diagnosis; **select by validation, not public**; **alpha/r=4**; **keep failed/low-confidence traces** (A/B vs our verified-only); equation candidate-ordering + two-axis guess; **re-test the equation premise**.
**Too expensive / not worth (skip):** curriculum learning (no benefit); two-stage training (redistributes, less stable than single-stage mixing); 3× priority (overfit); **relying on LoRA merge** (failed here — member-dependent); cryptarithm add/sub/mul traces (too jumpy to learn — needs LB1/LB3's structure instead).
```

```markdown
# Next-version plan — `lb10-v1`

> Post-competition plan derived from the **10th Place Solution** (Public 0.860 / Private 0.880).
> **Status: PLAN ONLY.** No GPU training, no Kaggle submit, no kernel push, no dataset upload now
> (`allow_* = false`; competition ended). Anchors: `gap_analysis.md`, `score_tricks.md`, `method_summary.md`, `../writeup/lb10-writeup.md`.

## Version name
`lb10-v1`

## Hypothesis
Most of our headroom is in the **deterministic teacher**, not SFT tuning: matching the bit reasoner to the true generator (a **rotate/shift key-table**) and adding **oracle-ceiling-vs-fidelity + logprob learnability** diagnosis will lift bit toward ~98% and make our imitation gaps visible. Two LB10 results directly challenge our practice and are worth A/B testing: **keeping failed/low-confidence traces** (LB10: excluding them hurt) and **not relying on LoRA merge** (LB10: merge failed). Plus the equation-deduce premise re-test (5th refutation).

## What we borrow from LB10
- **"Improve the teacher" discipline** — measure and raise per-category **oracle coverage** first; treat it as the score ceiling.
- **Rotate/shift key-table bit reasoner**: `out[i]=F(rotl(x,a),shl(x,b),shr(x,c))`, F read from examples as a 3-bit-key→bit table; recover `(a,b,c)` from boundary bits (bit0 shr=0, bit7 shl=0); compact `key>value` traces; gate extra scans by a threshold.
- **equation**: deduce candidate reorder by frequency; guess two-axis rebuild (operation = conventional-if-free else first-unused of {add, unsigned abs-diff, mul}; wrapper pinned from the most-example seen operator).
- **Validation**: 950 held-out per category; **oracle-ceiling vs model-fidelity** split; **per-example/per-epoch logprob learnability**; **select by validation, not public LB**.
- **Training**: alpha/r=4; priority 2× for fragile modes; add low-logprob problems + failure-mode demos and retrain.
- **Keep failed / low-confidence (`rule_unknown`) traces** (don't filter to solver-correct only).

## What new ideas we add (beyond LB10)
- **A/B our c1/c2 verified-only filter vs LB10's keep-failures** on our data — settle whether our filter discards useful signal.
- **A/B LoRA merge** under LB10's negative result vs our +0.01 and LB5's iterative soup — characterize when soup helps (member complementarity, averaging target).
- **Graft cryptarithm** from LB1 (signature catalog) / LB3 (CSP + two-stage) — LB10's cryptarithm is only 9% (add/sub/mul too jumpy); the top-end lever is a real cryptarithm solver.
- **Equation-deduce re-crack (no GPU)** — shared with `lb{1,3,5,6}-v1`.

## Data / corpus plan
- Program-generated deterministic traces per category; prompt-masked; >8192-token filter. Keep failed/low-conf traces (tagged `rule_unknown`). Priority 2× fragile modes; add low-logprob problems. No weights/large data in git.

## Prompt format
- Compact deterministic CoT ending `\boxed{}`; remove per-example echoes + candidate enumeration to avoid runaway loops; `key>value` rendering.

## Solver / synthetic generation plan
1. `bit_keytable_reasoner.py`: rotate/shift key-table; boundary-bit (a,b,c) recovery; conflict-pruned key-table accumulation; agreement/majority fallback; compact traces.
2. `equation_solver.py`: frequency-ordered deduce; two-axis guess; wrapper pinning.
3. `gen_*.py`: per-category generators; keep failed/low-conf traces.
4. `learnability.py`: per-example/per-epoch logprob export to find fragile traces.

## Training config (when GPU authorized — NOT now)
- Base Nemotron-3-Nano-30B; LoRA rank 32 / **alpha 128 (alpha/r=4)**; all-proj + lm_head; LR 2e-4 linear; **2 epochs**; eff batch 32; stratified.
- **Down-scale for post-comp RTX Pro 6000**: a few-category run validating the **bit key-table oracle lift** + the **keep-failures A/B** + **merge A/B** ≈ **8-16h**. Validate the *mechanism*, not full coverage.

## Validation plan (incl. T12 hard-val)
- **Primary**: 950 held-out per category; **oracle-ceiling vs model-fidelity** split; logprob learnability.
- **Secondary**: T12 hard-val (hard-tail hint; INS-002).
- **Select by validation**, never public; check cross-category regressions per change.

## Local official-like metric / extraction checks
- `\boxed{}` exact / rel-1e-2; "correct within 7680/8192 tokens"; per-category oracle coverage + model-vs-oracle fidelity; logprob histograms.

## Submit / no-submit gate
- **Competition over → no live submission; gate N/A now.** Future live: select by validation; ship the higher-validation run even if public is lower (LB10's lesson).

## Expected upside
- Bit toward ~98% (key-table). Equation toward ~93% deduce. Diagnosis (oracle vs fidelity, logprob) unblocks targeted fixes. Cryptarithm needs LB1/LB3 grafts. Realistically post-comp we validate the **mechanism** (bit key-table lift, keep-failures A/B, merge A/B), not full coverage.

## Risks
- **Cryptarithm** stays low without a real solver (LB10 = 9%).
- **Equation premise** (unlikely to hold after 5 refutations) — cheap to check.
- **Keep-failures A/B** may not replicate on our data/pipeline.
- **Merge A/B** is confounded (member complementarity); design carefully.
- **Compute** for the full teacher rebuild.

## GPU time estimate (for a future authorized run)
- LB10 reference: single base model, LoRA, 2 epochs, eff batch 32 (Kaggle-class). Our down-scaled validation ≈ **8-16h** on the RTX Pro 6000. Reasoner/generation prep: CPU, hours.

## Implementation checklist
- [ ] No-GPU: equation-deduce re-crack (shared with `lb{1,3,5,6}-v1`).
- [ ] Build `bit_keytable_reasoner.py` (boundary-bit recovery) + measure oracle lift.
- [ ] Build `equation_solver.py` (frequency-order deduce + two-axis guess).
- [ ] Build `learnability.py` (logprob export) + oracle-vs-fidelity reporting.
- [ ] A/B keep-failures vs verified-only (our c1/c2).
- [ ] A/B LoRA merge (characterize when soup helps).
- [ ] (GPU-gated) down-scaled run (alpha/r=4, 2 epochs); record under `runs/`.
- [ ] Select by validation; check per-category regressions.

## Rollback / hold-best strategy
- **Hold-best = our soup (Public 0.86 / Private 0.85)** + post-deadline **eq-aug (0.86/0.86)**. Any `lb10-v1` artifact must beat these on the offline metric before consideration; on regression, **revert to held-best** and keep `lb10-v1` as a documented method experiment. All work on a branch / under `runs/`; no held-best overwrite; no force-push.
```

```
13th Place Solution — NVIDIA Nemotron Model Reasoning Challenge
NVIDIA Nemotron Model Reasoning Challenge


Solution Writeup · 13th place · Jun 19, 2026
First, I would like to sincerely thank the organizers for hosting such an insightful and educational
competition. I also greatly appreciate the Kaggle community for sharing valuable discussions
and open-source code, which were highly informative throughout the competition. My approach
focused primarily on training data construction and iterative refinement. Special thanks to
@huikang for releasing a highly polished and well-designed dataset generation pipeline in the
Open Progress Prize Publication, which served as the foundation of my approach.

Overview & Key Approach
To improve the accuracy of teacher-generated Chain-of-Thought (CoT) traces, I built upon the
reasoners released in the Open Progress Prize Publication and introduced several task-specific
heuristics that increased the proportion of correctly solved training examples.

Performance Summary

         Category       Found Total Accuracy
bit_manipulation        1,437 1,602 89.7%
cipher                  1,576 1,576 100.0%
cryptarithm_deduce      66    659 10.0%
cryptarithm_guess       13    164 7.9%
equation_numeric_deduce 568 596 95.3%
equation_numeric_guess 69     136 50.7%
gravity                 1,597 1,597 100.0%
numeral                 1,576 1,576 100.0%
unit_conversion         1,594 1,594 100.0%
TOTAL                   8,496 9,500 89.4%

Note: Overall accuracy increased from 87.7% to 89.4%, with major
improvements achieved in equation_numeric_guess, equation_numeric_deduce,
and bit_manipulation.

Reasoner Modifications by Category
1. bit_manipulation

Key Enhancements

   •   Added explicit verification of 3-input operations, specifically MAJORITY and XNOR.
   •   Restricted the search space using inferred input bit-position information derived from the
       left and right operands.
   •   Implemented left-edge propagation as the default fallback rule when no valid operation
       was found.
   •   Removed the parsing-display section to free token budget for the additional verification
       process.

2. cryptarithm

Output Format Simplification

Reduced syntax ambiguity caused by extra braces appearing in final answers:

   •   Old: output: 【%&$>】 -> 【{%&$>}】
   •   New: output: 【%&$>】

Robust Aggregation

After parsing both the examples and the target problem, the solver collects statistics on usage
patterns of the target operator (e.g., consistency with concatenation or reverse concatenation). To
mitigate symbol transcription errors, an operation is treated as a valid candidate if it matches at
least one relevant example, rather than requiring strict consistency across all examples.

Fallback Strategy

When examples using the target operator are available, the solver evaluates both concatenation
and reverse concatenation.
If neither yields a unique solution:

   1. Collect all symbols.
   2. Identify operator symbols vs. non-operator symbols.
   3. Return the first remaining non-operator symbol as the final answer.
      This removes logical contradictions where concatenation was incorrectly applied to tasks
      for which the examples already demonstrated that it was inappropriate.

Dataset Rebalancing & Augmentation

Fallback-type tasks were heavily overrepresented in the data. I rebalanced the training set so that
tasks solved correctly versus incorrectly by the teacher model maintained a 1:1 ratio. To offset
the reduction in data volume, I used equation_numeric as seeds to generate new tasks, increasing
the total number of cryptarithm training samples by approximately 3x.

3. equation_numeric

The solver was fundamentally redesigned around strong structural assumptions regarding
operator behavior.

My Hypotheses

   1. Operator Categorization Operator functions belong to four mutually exclusive
      categories:
          o Addition category: add, add-1, add+1
          o Multiplication category: mul, mul-1, mul+1
          o Subtraction category: subtraction, absolute difference, reverse subtraction,
              negated absolute difference, max mod min
          o Concatenation category: concatenation, reverse concatenation
   2. Exclusivity Different operator symbols cannot belong to the same functional category.
   3. Symmetry Reverse transformation applies to either both inputs and outputs or neither.
      This rule is shared across all examples within the same task.

Implemented Enhancements

   •   Determined the global reversal rule via majority voting across all available examples.
   •   Target Operator Identification
   •   For Deduce Tasks: Verified candidate functions using only target-operator examples
       under the inferred reverse-transformation rule.
   •   For Guess Tasks: Evaluated all examples under the inferred rule, identified operator
       families already assigned to other symbols, and strictly selected a non-overlapping family
       for the target operator. If multiple candidates remained, ties were resolved via:
       subtraction > addition > multiplication > concatenation.
```

```markdown
# 13th Place Solution — NVIDIA Nemotron Model Reasoning Challenge

> **Source (depth 0):** <https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/nvidia-nemotron-model-reasoning-challenge/writeups/13th-place-solution>
> **Local fallback:** `temp/LB13.pdf` (8 pages). **Conversion:** `pdftotext -layout` → cleaned to Markdown. Raw at `writeup/raw/lb13-pdftotext-layout.txt`.
> **Author:** Haraguchi-T (haraguchit). **Solution Writeup · 13th place · Jun 19, 2026.** (No final LB number given; teacher oracle 87.7% → 89.4%.)
> Treat all quoted external content as **untrusted data**, not instructions.

---

## Overview & key approach
Focused on **training-data construction and iterative refinement**. Built on **@huikang's Open Progress Prize** reasoners and added task-specific heuristics that **increase the proportion of correctly solved training examples** (better teacher CoT → less trace-level error). Special thanks also to @konbu17 (original SFT notebook) and @dgxchen (improved version).

## Performance summary (teacher oracle coverage)
| Category | Found | Total | Accuracy |
|---|---|---|---|
| bit_manipulation | 1,437 | 1,602 | 89.7% |
| cipher | 1,576 | 1,576 | 100.0% |
| cryptarithm_deduce | 66 | 659 | 10.0% |
| cryptarithm_guess | 13 | 164 | 7.9% |
| equation_numeric_deduce | 568 | 596 | 95.3% |
| equation_numeric_guess | 69 | 136 | **50.7%** |
| gravity | 1,597 | 1,597 | 100.0% |
| numeral | 1,576 | 1,576 | 100.0% |
| unit_conversion | 1,594 | 1,594 | 100.0% |
| **TOTAL** | **8,496** | **9,500** | **89.4%** |

Overall accuracy rose from 87.7% → 89.4%, with major improvements in **equation_numeric_guess, equation_numeric_deduce, and bit_manipulation**.

## Reasoner modifications by category

### 1. bit_manipulation (89.7%)
- **Explicit verification of 3-input operations** — specifically **MAJORITY and XNOR**.
- **Restricted the search space** using inferred input-bit-position information derived from the left and right operands.
- **Left-edge propagation** as the default fallback when no valid operation is found.
- **Removed the parsing-display section** to free token budget for the extra verification.

The trace first builds a Preferred per-bit assignment, then for any unresolved bit (`none`) runs **3-input matching** over MAJ/XNOR candidates (printing each candidate's per-example bit columns and the bit it matches), selects the matching 3-input op (e.g. `2 XNOR157`), and finalizes the 8-bit Selected rule.

### 2. cryptarithm (deduce 10.0%)
- **Output format simplification** — remove extra braces in final answers: `output: 【%&$>】 -> 【{%&$>}】` → `output: 【%&$>】` (reduce syntax ambiguity).
- **Robust aggregation** — after parsing examples + target, collect target-operator usage statistics (e.g. consistency with concat / reverse-concat); to mitigate **symbol transcription errors**, treat an operation as a valid candidate if it matches **at least one** relevant example rather than requiring strict consistency across **all**.
- **Fallback strategy** — when target-operator examples exist, evaluate both concat and reverse-concat; if neither yields a unique solution: (1) collect all symbols; (2) split operator vs non-operator symbols; (3) return the **first remaining non-operator symbol** as the answer (removes contradictions where concat was wrongly applied).
- **Dataset rebalancing & augmentation** — fallback-type tasks were heavily overrepresented; **rebalanced so teacher-correct : teacher-incorrect = 1:1**. To offset the volume reduction, used **equation_numeric as seeds** to generate new cryptarithm tasks, **~3× more cryptarithm training samples**.

### 3. equation_numeric (deduce 95.3%, guess 50.7%)
Redesigned around **strong structural assumptions**:
1. **Operator categorization** — four mutually exclusive categories: **Addition** (add, add−1, add+1), **Multiplication** (mul, mul−1, mul+1), **Subtraction** (subtraction, absolute difference, reverse subtraction, negated absolute difference, max-mod-min), **Concatenation** (concat, reverse concat).
2. **Exclusivity** — different operator symbols cannot belong to the same functional category.
3. **Symmetry** — reverse transformation applies to **either both inputs and outputs or neither**, and this rule is **shared across all examples within a task**.

Enhancements:
- **Global reversal rule via majority voting** across all examples (the trace tries `(rev_ops, rev_res)` combinations per operator example, tallies votes, picks the winner — e.g. `(False,False)=3` beats `(True,True)=0`).
- **Deduce** — verify candidate functions using **only target-operator examples** under the inferred reverse rule.
- **Guess** — evaluate all examples under the inferred rule, identify operator **families already assigned** to other symbols, and **strictly select a non-overlapping family** for the target; ties resolved by **subtraction > addition > multiplication > concatenation**.

(The writeup includes detailed traces: a "Detect reversal pattern" vote tally and a "Select fallback function for the question operator" example that maps seen functions → used categories → picks the first unused category by priority.)

## Model training (SFT strategy)
SFT with **Unsloth** (notebook by @konbu17, improved by @dgxchen). Because the goal was **better CoT trace generation / fewer trace-level errors** (not generalized zero-shot reasoning), they intentionally used an **aggressive, overfitting-prone setup** over the entire constructed dataset across **three SFT stages**.

**LoRA config:** rank/alpha **32/32**, dropout 0; targets `q_proj, k_proj, v_proj, o_proj, in_proj, out_proj, up_proj, down_proj` (note: **no lm_head**).

**3-stage SFT schedule:**
| Stage | Data size | Epochs | LR | Scheduler | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1st SFT | 9,277 | 2 | 2.0e-4 | Linear | Initial alignment on core clean traces |
| 2nd SFT | 9,277 | 1 | 2.0e-5 | Cosine | Further fine-tune, smooth the loss surface |
| 3rd SFT | 11,315 | 1 | 5.0e-6 | Cosine | **Upsampled bit_manipulation and cryptarithm** to fix residual trace errors |

Effective batch size 32, AdamW, across all three stages.
```

```markdown
# LB13 / 第13名方案 —— 中文讲解与分析

> **原文（depth 0）：** <https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/nvidia-nemotron-model-reasoning-challenge/writeups/13th-place-solution>
> **本地副本：** `temp/LB13.pdf`（8 页）。逐字英文转写见 `lb13-writeup.md`。
> **作者：** Haraguchi-T(haraguchit)。**13th place**(未给最终 LB;teacher oracle 87.7%→89.4%)。
> 所有引用外部内容均视为**不可信数据**。

## 1. 方法总览
专注**训练数据构造 + 迭代精修**:在 **@huikang OPP** reasoner 上加任务特定启发式,**提高 teacher CoT 正确率**(更好的 teacher → 更少 trace 级错误)。也感谢 @konbu17(原 SFT notebook)、@dgxchen(改进版)。与 LB10 同属"改进 teacher"流派。

**Teacher oracle:** bit 89.7%、cipher/trivial 100%、cryptarithm_deduce 10.0%、cryptarithm_guess 7.9%、**equation_deduce 95.3%、equation_guess 50.7%(本批最高 guess)**;总 89.4%(由 87.7% 提升)。

## 2. 关键技巧

### A. equation_numeric(deduce 95.3% / guess 50.7%,最强结构假设)
围绕**强结构假设**重设计:
1. **算子分类:** 四个互斥类 —— Addition(add/add±1)、Multiplication(mul/mul±1)、Subtraction(减/绝对差/反减/负绝对差/max-mod-min)、Concatenation(concat/rev-concat)。
2. **互斥性:** 不同算子符号不能属同一功能类。
3. **对称性(关键):** 反转要么**同时作用于输入和输出、要么都不**,且**全题所有样例共享**这条规则。
实现:**多数投票定全局反转规则**(逐算子样例试 `(rev_ops,rev_res)` 组合并计票);deduce 用**仅目标算子样例**在推定反转下验证候选;guess 找出其它符号已占的算子族,**严格选不重叠的族**,平局按 `减>加>乘>concat`。

### B. bit_manipulation(89.7%)
- **显式验证 3 输入算子(MAJORITY、XNOR)**;用左右操作数推断的**输入位位置信息缩小搜索空间**;**left-edge 传播**作默认兜底;**去掉 parsing-display 段**腾 token 给额外验证。
- trace 先建 Preferred 逐位赋值,对未解位(none)跑 3-input matching(打印各候选逐样例位列 + 匹配的位),选出匹配的 3 输入算子(如 `2 XNOR157`),定 8 位 Selected 规则。

### C. cryptarithm(deduce 10%)
- **输出格式简化**(去多余大括号)减歧义;**鲁棒聚合**:为缓解**符号转写错误**,某操作只要匹配**≥1 个**相关样例即视为候选(而非要求**全部**严格一致);**兜底**:若 concat/rev-concat 都不唯一 → 收集所有符号、分算子/非算子符号、返回**第一个剩余非算子符号**。
- **数据再平衡:teacher 答对:答错 = 1:1**(fallback 类原本超量);用 equation_numeric 作种子造新 cryptarithm,**样本量 ~3×**。

### D. SFT(3 阶段,递减 LR)
Unsloth(@konbu17 notebook、@dgxchen 改进)。目标是**改善 CoT trace 生成**而非零样本泛化 → **故意激进、易过拟合**。LoRA rank/alpha 32/32、dropout 0、targets q/k/v/o + in/out + up/down(**无 lm_head**)。
- **stage1:** 9,277、2 epoch、LR 2e-4 linear(核心干净 trace 对齐)。
- **stage2:** 9,277、1 epoch、LR 2e-5 cosine(平滑损失面)。
- **stage3:** 11,315、1 epoch、LR 5e-6 cosine(**上采样 bit + cryptarithm** 修残余 trace 错)。
eff batch 32、AdamW。

## 3. 对我们可复用

| 技巧 | 可复用 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| **equation 三假设(分类/互斥/对称)+ 多数投票定反转** | ✅ 最高价值、且**第 6 次反驳我方 EQ 误判** | guess 50.7%(全批最高)、deduce 95.3%。"反转全题共享 + 互斥族"是最锐利的 equation 结构模型。见下。 |
| **数据再平衡 1:1 答对:答错** | ✅ **印证 LB10、挑战我方 c1/c2** | LB13 **保留答错 trace** 并按 1:1 平衡;与 LB10"剔除失败掉点"一致。我方 c1/c2 只留答对 → 应 A/B。 |
| **鲁棒聚合(匹配 ≥1 例而非全部)** | ✅ | 缓解符号转写/噪声;我方严格一致可能丢候选。 |
| **3 阶段递减 LR SFT(2e-4→2e-5→5e-6)** | ✅ | 先对齐、再平滑、末段上采样难类修残错;比单次 SFT 更精修 trace。 |
| bit 3 输入验证(MAJ/XNOR)+ 位位置缩搜索 + left-edge 兜底 | ✅ | 我方 bit ~10%;3 输入验证是覆盖率关键。 |
| **改进 teacher 而非超参** 哲学 | ✅ | 与 LB10 一致:分数被 teacher oracle 上限框住。 |
| cryptarithm 输出格式去括号 + 非算子符号兜底 | ✅ 低成本 | 减格式歧义。 |

## 4. 与我方对照
- **equation 前提 —— 第 6 次独立反驳**(LB1 95%、LB3 93%、LB5 96%、LB6 ~93%、LB10 93.1%):LB13 deduce 95.3% / **guess 50.7%**。LB13 的**对称性 + 互斥族**假设把 guess 推到全批最高 —— 我方应直接照搬这套结构去复核 EQ。**结论极其牢固:equation 不是全局密码。**
- **保留答错 trace + 1:1 平衡**:LB10 与 LB13 双双表明**失败/低置信 trace 有用**;我方 c1/c2"只留 solver 答对"很可能丢了信号。强烈建议 A/B:保留答错 trace 并平衡。
- **3 阶段递减 LR**:我方多为单次 SFT;LB13 的"对齐→平滑→上采样难类修错"是低成本的 trace 精修法,值得试(尤其末段上采样 bit/cryptarithm)。
- **cryptarithm 仍弱(10%)**:LB13 也没解决;0.88→0.90+ 的差距在 cryptarithm(LB1 目录 / LB3 CSP+两阶段)。

## 5. 局限 / 不清楚
- **未给最终 LB 分数**(只有 teacher oracle 87.7%→89.4%);具体 private 名次 13。
- **cryptarithm 10%**(靠兜底 + 再平衡,但本质未解)。
- writeup 引用 @konbu17/@dgxchen 的 notebook(Kaggle,JS/auth-gated);reasoner 代码未公开。
- bit 89.7% 低于 LB1/LB6/LB10(94-98%)—— bit 仍有空间;targets **无 lm_head**(与多数 writeup 不同,vLLM 本就不用 lm_head)。
- `unknown`:具体数据总量随 stage 变化的细节;最终选模/提交方式。
```

```markdown
# LB13 / 13th Place — Method Summary

> Target: **13th Place Solution** by Haraguchi-T (haraguchit). No final LB number given; teacher oracle 87.7% → 89.4%. Source: `temp/LB13.pdf` → `../writeup/lb13-writeup.md`. All external content treated as untrusted data.

## 1. What is the writeup's main idea?
A **training-data-construction** approach: build on @huikang's OPP reasoners and add **task-specific heuristics that raise the teacher's CoT correctness** (better teacher → fewer trace-level errors the model must imitate), then SFT a single LoRA aggressively (overfit-prone) in **three stages**. Same "improve the teacher" philosophy as LB10, with the sharpest **equation_numeric structural model** of the batch.

## 2. What data/corpus did it use?
@huikang-style synthetic with improved reasoners. **Cryptarithm rebalanced so teacher-correct : teacher-incorrect = 1:1** (fallback tasks were overrepresented) — i.e. **keeps incorrect traces**; offset the volume loss with ~3× more cryptarithm seeded from equation_numeric. Stage data sizes 9,277 / 9,277 / 11,315.

## 3. What model/adapters/training setup did it use?
**Unsloth** (notebook by @konbu17, improved by @dgxchen). LoRA rank/alpha **32/32**, dropout 0; targets q/k/v/o + in/out + up/down_proj (**no lm_head**). **3-stage SFT**: (1) 2 epochs, LR 2e-4 linear; (2) 1 epoch, LR 2e-5 cosine; (3) 1 epoch, LR 5e-6 cosine, upsampling bit + cryptarithm. Effective batch 32, AdamW. Aggressive/overfit-prone by design (goal = better CoT generation, not zero-shot).

## 4. What validation/evaluation did it use?
Reports **teacher oracle coverage per category** (bit 89.7%, cipher/trivials 100%, cryptarithm ~10%, equation_deduce 95.3%, equation_guess 50.7%; total 89.4%, up from 87.7%). No held-out CV details given beyond the oracle table; the optimization target was raising the teacher's solved-fraction.

## 5. What were the most important score-improvement tricks?
(Full table in `score_tricks.md`.) 1) **equation_numeric structural redesign** — 4 mutually-exclusive operator categories + exclusivity + **reversal symmetry shared across all examples**, global reversal by **majority vote**, family-exclusion guess (ties: sub > add > mul > concat) → deduce 95.3%, **guess 50.7% (highest in the batch)**. 2) **bit 3-input verification** (MAJORITY/XNOR) + bit-position-restricted search + left-edge fallback + drop parsing-display → 89.7%. 3) **Dataset rebalancing to 1:1 correct:incorrect** (keeps failed traces). 4) **Robust aggregation** (op valid if it matches ≥1 example, not all — handles symbol transcription errors). 5) **3-stage decreasing-LR SFT** (2e-4 → 2e-5 → 5e-6, upsample hard categories last).

## 6. What failure modes did the author avoid?
- **Avoided** strict all-example consistency (robust aggregation tolerates transcription noise).
- **Avoided** discarding teacher-incorrect traces (rebalanced 1:1 instead — keeping them).
- **Avoided** cryptarithm logical contradictions (non-operator-symbol fallback; format de-bracing).
- **Avoided** a single coarse SFT (3-stage: align → smooth → upsample-hard).

## 7. What makes this different from public 0.85/0.86 baselines and our attempts?
- The **sharpest equation_numeric structural model** in this batch (reversal symmetry + family exclusivity), giving the **highest guess rate (50.7%)** — the **6th independent refutation** of our "equation = global cipher" verdict.
- vs **us**: LB13 **keeps teacher-incorrect traces and balances them 1:1** (echoing LB10's "excluding failed traces hurts") — our c1/c2 keep **only solver-correct** rows, so we likely discard useful signal. # LB13 / 13th Place — Score-improvement tricks
```

```markdown
> Evidence cites `../writeup/lb13-writeup.md` (= `temp/LB13.pdf`). "reusable by us" judged vs our repo (notes.md / submissions.md / equation-frontier.md).

| trick | description | evidence | likely impact | reusable by us? | difficulty |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **equation structural redesign (3 assumptions)** | 4 mutually-exclusive operator categories (add/mul/sub/concat); exclusivity (distinct symbols ≠ same category); **reversal symmetry shared across all examples**. Global reversal via majority vote; deduce verifies via target-operator examples; guess strictly picks an unused family (ties sub>add>mul>concat). | §3 equation; deduce 95.3%, **guess 50.7%** | **High** (equation; highest guess in batch) | **Yes — adopt for our EQ; re-check premise** | Medium |
| **Dataset rebalancing 1:1 correct:incorrect** | Rebalance teacher-correct vs teacher-incorrect traces to 1:1 (fallback overrepresented); keeps incorrect traces. | §2 cryptarithm | **Medium-High** | **Yes — challenges our c1/c2 verified-only** (echoes LB10) | Low |
| **Robust aggregation (match ≥1 example)** | An operation is a valid candidate if it matches ≥1 relevant example, not all — tolerates symbol transcription errors. | §2 cryptarithm | **Medium** | **Yes** | Low |
| **bit 3-input verification (MAJORITY/XNOR)** | Explicitly verify 3-input ops for unresolved bits; restrict search via input-bit-position from left/right operands; left-edge propagation fallback; drop parsing-display to free tokens. | §1 bit; 89.7% | **Medium-High** (bit) | **Yes** — our bit ~10% | Medium |
| **3-stage decreasing-LR SFT** | Stage1 LR 2e-4 linear 2ep (align); stage2 2e-5 cosine 1ep (smooth); stage3 5e-6 cosine 1ep (upsample bit+cryptarithm). | §SFT | **Medium** | **Yes — cheap A/B vs single-stage** | Low-Medium |
| **Aggressive/overfit-prone SFT for CoT fidelity** | Goal = better CoT trace generation, not zero-shot → use the entire dataset, overfit-prone. | §SFT | **Medium** | **Yes** (trace-fidelity framing) | Low |
| **cryptarithm output de-bracing + non-operator-symbol fallback** | Remove extra braces (syntax ambiguity); if concat/rev-concat non-unique, return first remaining non-operator symbol. | §2 cryptarithm | **Low-Medium** | **Yes** | Low |
| **equation augmentation as cryptarithm seeds** | Use equation_numeric problems as seeds to 3× cryptarithm samples. | §2 cryptarithm | **Low-Medium** | **Yes** | Low |
| **LoRA targets without lm_head** | Targets q/k/v/o + in/out + up/down (no lm_head). | §SFT | **Low** (vLLM ignores lm_head anyway) | **Yes** (consistent with LB5 note) | Low |
```
