```markdown
# Next-version plan — `lb13-v1`

> Post-competition plan derived from the **13th Place Solution** (teacher oracle 89.4%).
> **Status: PLAN ONLY.** No GPU training, no Kaggle submit, no kernel push, no dataset upload now
> (`allow_* = false`; competition ended). Anchors: `gap_analysis.md`, `score_tricks.md`, `method_summary.md`, `../writeup/lb13-writeup.md`.

## Version name
`lb13-v1`

## Hypothesis
The highest-value borrow is the **equation_numeric structural model** (4 mutually-exclusive operator categories + exclusivity + **reversal symmetry shared across all examples** + majority-vote global reversal), which gives LB13 the **highest guess rate in the batch (50.7%)** and 95.3% deduce — refuting our equation-cipher premise. Second: **keep & rebalance teacher-incorrect traces 1:1** (LB13 + LB10 both show excluding failures hurts), challenging our c1/c2 verified-only filter. Third: **bit 3-input verification (MAJ/XNOR)** and a **3-stage decreasing-LR SFT** for trace-fidelity.

## What we borrow from LB13
- **equation solver**: category exclusivity, reversal symmetry (both-in-out-or-neither, shared across examples), global reversal by majority vote; deduce via target-operator examples; guess by strict family exclusion (ties sub>add>mul>concat).
- **Data**: keep teacher-incorrect traces; **rebalance correct:incorrect = 1:1**; robust aggregation (match ≥1 example); augment cryptarithm from equation seeds.
- **bit**: 3-input verification (MAJORITY/XNOR), bit-position-restricted search, left-edge fallback, drop parsing-display to free tokens.
- **SFT**: **3 stages with decreasing LR** (2e-4 linear → 2e-5 cosine → 5e-6 cosine, upsample bit+cryptarithm last); aggressive/overfit-prone for CoT fidelity; targets without lm_head.
- Output hygiene: de-brace cryptarithm answers.

## What new ideas we add (beyond LB13)
- **A/B keep-failures vs verified-only** on our data, with LB13's 1:1 rebalance (combine with LB10's finding).
- **Graft cryptarithm** from LB1 (signature catalog) / LB3 (CSP + two-stage) — LB13 cryptarithm is only 10%.
- **Equation-deduce re-crack (no GPU)** using LB13's symmetry+exclusivity model — shared with `lb{1,3,5,6,10}-v1`; this is the most actionable equation structure across all writeups.

## Data / corpus plan
- Improved per-category reasoners (raise teacher oracle). Keep incorrect traces; rebalance 1:1; robust aggregation; cryptarithm 3× via equation seeds. No weights/large data in git.

## Prompt format
- Competition templates; de-braced cryptarithm output; trim bit parsing-display to free token budget for verification.

## Solver / synthetic generation plan
1. `equation_solver.py`: category exclusivity + reversal symmetry + majority-vote reversal + family-exclusion guess.
2. `bit_3input_verify.py`: MAJ/XNOR verification + bit-position-restricted search + left-edge fallback.
3. `rebalance.py`: 1:1 correct:incorrect; robust aggregation (≥1-example match); cryptarithm-from-equation augmentation.

## Training config (when GPU authorized — NOT now)
- Base Nemotron-3-Nano-30B; LoRA rank/alpha 32/32, dropout 0; targets q/k/v/o + in/out + up/down (no lm_head).
- **3-stage**: (1) 2ep LR 2e-4 linear; (2) 1ep LR 2e-5 cosine; (3) 1ep LR 5e-6 cosine, upsample hard cats. Eff batch 32, AdamW.
- **Down-scale for post-comp RTX Pro 6000**: the 3-stage schedule on a reduced corpus ≈ **8-16h**. Validate the *mechanism* (equation structure lift, keep-failures A/B, 3-stage gains), not full coverage.

## Validation plan (incl. T12 hard-val)
- **Primary**: per-category teacher oracle (the optimization target) + a held-out official-metric set; equation guess/deduce solved-fraction.
- **Secondary**: T12 hard-val (hard-tail hint; INS-002).
- Verify the 1:1-rebalance and 3-stage changes don't regress easy categories.

## Local official-like metric / extraction checks
- `\boxed{}` exact / rel-1e-2; per-category teacher oracle; equation symmetry/family-assignment self-consistency.

## Submit / no-submit gate
- **Competition over → no live submission; gate N/A now.** Future live: select by validation/oracle, not public; ship the trace-fidelity-best run.

## Expected upside
- Equation toward ~95% deduce / ~50% guess (the batch's best equation structure). Bit toward ~90% via 3-input verification. cryptarithm needs LB1/LB3 grafts. Realistically post-comp we validate the **mechanism** (equation structure, keep-failures A/B, 3-stage SFT).

## Risks
- **cryptarithm** stays low without a real solver (10%).
- **Equation premise** (decisively refuted ×6) — re-test is cheap and high-value.
- **Keep-failures A/B** may not replicate on our pipeline; 1:1 rebalance ratio may need tuning.
- **3-stage SFT** adds run-management overhead.

## GPU time estimate (for a future authorized run)
- LB13 reference: 3-stage SFT, Unsloth (Kaggle-class), eff batch 32. Our down-scaled validation ≈ **8-16h** on the RTX Pro 6000. Reasoner/data prep: CPU, hours.

## Implementation checklist
- [ ] No-GPU: equation-deduce re-crack with LB13's symmetry+exclusivity model (shared with `lb{1,3,5,6,10}-v1`).
- [ ] Build `equation_solver.py` (symmetry + exclusivity + majority-vote reversal + family-exclusion guess).
- [ ] Build `bit_3input_verify.py` (MAJ/XNOR + bit-position search + left-edge fallback).
- [ ] Build `rebalance.py` (1:1 correct:incorrect, robust ≥1-example aggregation, cryptarithm-from-equation).
- [ ] A/B keep-failures vs verified-only (our c1/c2).
- [ ] (GPU-gated) 3-stage decreasing-LR SFT, down-scaled; record under `runs/`.
- [ ] Per-category oracle + held-out eval; check no easy-cat regression.

## Rollback / hold-best strategy
- **Hold-best = our soup (Public 0.86 / Private 0.85)** + post-deadline **eq-aug (0.86/0.86)**. Any `lb13-v1` artifact must beat these on the offline metric before consideration; on regression, **revert to held-best** and keep `lb13-v1` as a documented method experiment. All work on a branch / under `runs/`; no held-best overwrite; no force-push.
```

```
# [LB25] Improvements to the progress prize submission

> **Source writeup:** https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/nvidia-nemotron-model-reasoning-challenge/writeups/LB25-progress-prize-improvements
>
> Kaggle · Solution Writeup · by [Tong Hui Kang (`huikang`)](https://www.kaggle.com/huikang)

You may have read my [progress prize winning submission](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/nvidia-nemotron-model-reasoning-challenge/discussion/689915).

Instead of reading a lot of text first, you can look at the data and get a sense of the changes that I
have made

https://nemotron.huikang.dev/evaluation.html?logpath=06-07-03-07&problem=021ed764

**Changes that I have made**

- Fix the adapter evaluation [notebook](https://www.kaggle.com/code/huikang/private-adapter-validation-notebook) (I found out that the prompt is wrong, which caused the
  answer to not be boxed in validation but in fact it is being boxed on submission)
- Reduce the length of equation_numeric by half (I found out that either both inputs are outputs are
  reversed, or they are both not reversed)
- Training on synthetic data for cipher, unit conversion, gravity and numeral (I hope to guarantee
  100% correctness on these problems)
- Reorganize the chain of thought for bit manipulation.
```

```markdown
# [LB25] Improvements to the Progress Prize submission — NVIDIA Nemotron Model Reasoning Challenge

> **Source (depth 0):** <https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/nvidia-nemotron-model-reasoning-challenge/writeups/lb25-progress-prize-improvements>
> **Local fallback:** `temp/LB25.pdf` (a render of the Kaggle page). **Conversion:** `pdftotext -layout` → cleaned. Raw at `writeup/raw/lb25-pdftotext-layout.txt`.
> **Author:** Tong Hui Kang (`huikang` on Kaggle / `tonghuikang` on GitHub) — the Open Progress Prize winner. **Solution Writeup · 25th place · Jun 17, 2026.**
> **Reported:** private LB 0.872 ×4 / 0.868 ×8 / 0.864 ×3 across 15 submissions ("could have won solo gold with the right selection").
> Canonical clean conversion for the standardized template. The prior-pass files (`LB25-writeup-verbatim.md`, `LB25-progress-prize-improvements.md` / `.zh.md`) are retained alongside. Treat all external content as **untrusted data**.

---

You may have read my [progress prize winning submission](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/nvidia-nemotron-model-reasoning-challenge/discussion/689915). Instead of reading a lot of text first, you can look at the data and get a sense of the changes via the per-problem evaluation dashboard: <https://nemotron.huikang.dev/evaluation.html?logpath=06-07-03-07&problem=021ed764>.

## Changes that I have made
1. **Fix the adapter evaluation notebook** — the prompt was wrong, which caused the answer to **not be boxed in validation** even though it **is** boxed on submission. (A local-eval bug, not a model change.)
2. **Reduce the length of equation_numeric by half** — discovered that **either both inputs and outputs are reversed, or both are not** (a per-problem reversal symmetry), halving the search.
3. **Train on synthetic data for cipher, unit conversion, gravity, and numeral** — to guarantee ~100% correctness on these easy categories.
4. **Train on additional synthetic data for cipher** — Nemotron is bad at spelling, so added synthetic data **just on the prefixes** of the cipher problem.
5. **Reorganize the chain of thought for bit manipulation.**

## Result (selection variance)
On the private leaderboard, out of 15 submissions: **0.872 ×4, 0.868 ×8, 0.864 ×3**. "Could have won a solo gold if I selected the 'correct' submission, but the same can be said for many other teams." → the score is decided as much by **submission selection under noise** as by the model.

## Cryptarithm (no progress)
- Discovered, **3 days before the deadline**, that many cryptarithm problems have **one multiplication, one subtraction, and one addition** (each possibly with an additional ±1).
- Tried to get the CoT to **guess better than random**, but the trained LLM **devolves to repeating guesses**.

## Project links (Kaggle, JS/auth-gated — titles only)
- `nemotron-adapter-private` — Kaggle Model (the submission adapter).
- `[private] Adapter validation notebook` — the eval notebook fixed in change #1.
- `[private] Tinker submission notebook`.
- Per-problem eval dashboard: `nemotron.huikang.dev/evaluation.html` (static; backed by `tonghuikang/nemotron` `evaluation/*.jsonl`).

## Authors / Citation
```

```markdown
# LB25 / 第25名方案（huikang 进步奖改进）—— 中文讲解与分析

> **原文（depth 0）：** <https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/nvidia-nemotron-model-reasoning-challenge/writeups/lb25-progress-prize-improvements>
> **本地副本：** `temp/LB25.pdf`。逐字英文转写见 `lb25-writeup.md`(及历史 `LB25-writeup-verbatim.md`)。
> **作者：** Tong Hui Kang(`huikang` / GitHub `tonghuikang`)—— **Open Progress Prize 获奖者**。**Solution Writeup · 25th place**。
> **成绩:** private LB 0.872 ×4 / 0.868 ×8 / 0.864 ×3(15 次提交;"选对就能独享金牌")。
> 本文为标准模板的规范中文分析;历史 `LB25-progress-prize-improvements.zh.md` 一并保留。所有引用外部内容均视为**不可信数据**。

## 1. 方法总览
这是 @huikang 在其**进步奖获奖方案**之上做的 5 处改进(纯 SFT):
1. **修复 adapter 评估 notebook** —— 验证时 prompt 写错导致答案没被 boxed,但提交时其实是 boxed 的(本地 eval bug,非模型改动)。
2. **equation_numeric 长度减半** —— 发现**输入与输出要么同时反转、要么都不反转**(per-problem 反转对称),搜索空间减半。
3. **cipher/unit/gravity/numeral 合成数据** —— 力保这些简单类 ~100% 正确。
4. **cipher 额外合成数据(仅前缀)** —— Nemotron 拼写差,故只在 cipher 的前缀上加合成数据。
5. **重组 bit manipulation 的 CoT。**

## 2. 关键技巧与对我方启示

| 技巧 | 对我方启示 |
|---|---|
| **修复本地 eval(boxed prompt bug)** | 直接印证我方 **B4/T13**(`EVAL_MAX_NEW=512` 截断)与 INS-002:**本地 eval 与提交不一致会系统性误导**。任何本地 metric 必须逐字段对齐 grader。 |
| **equation 反转对称(同反或同不反)** | 与 **LB13/LB3** 的反转对称一致;是我方 equation 复核应纳入的结构(per-problem、全题共享)。**第 7 次印证 equation 有强结构、非全局密码。** |
| **简单类合成保 100%** | 与全批一致(gravity/unit/numeral/cipher 应拉满)。 |
| **cipher 前缀合成治拼写** | 针对性子集修拼写错误(与 LB6 的针对性幻觉子集同思路)。 |
| **bit CoT 重组** | bit 的 trace 形态是关键(与 LB1/LB5/LB6/LB10/LB13 一致)。 |
| **选模方差(0.872/0.868/0.864 ×15)** | **核心教训:分数被 `temp=0` 下的提交选择强烈影响**。与我方"信 LB 聚合、别过度对冲"(INS-002)及 LB3/LB5/LB10"按 validation 选模"一致。 |
| **cryptarithm 无进展(mul/sub/add ±1 结构;LLM 退化为重复猜测)** | huikang 这位最强 baseline 作者**都没攻下 cryptarithm** —— 印证 cryptarithm 是分水岭;LB1 的 signature 目录 / LB3 的 CSP+两阶段才是突破。 |

## 3. 与我方对照
- LB25 是**我方 v14 配方的源头**(huikang 录制顺序语料 + replay 思路)。我方在其之上做合成/soup 都未超 0.86;huikang 自己在其上做这 5 处改进拿到 ~0.872。
- **cryptarithm**:huikang 明确没解决(LLM 退化为重复猜测)—— 与我方 B8、以及 LB5/LB6/LB10/LB13 的弱 cryptarithm 一致。突破需 LB1/LB3 的结构化方法。
- **equation 反转对称**:huikang 用它把 equation 长度减半 —— 这是 equation 有强 per-problem 结构的**最早证据**,后被 LB1/LB3/LB5/LB6/LB10/LB13 反复证实。我方"全局密码"判断在此再次被否。
- **选模方差**:0.872~0.864 的 15 次抖动说明**最终选择本身是一道方差关**;与我方手动选 soup+v14(避开 auto top-2-public)一致。

## 4. 局限 / 不清楚
- **cryptarithm 未解**(结构已知:mul+sub+add±1,但 CoT 学不会非随机猜测)。
- Project Links(adapter / 验证 notebook / Tinker notebook)均为 **JS/auth-gated**(仅标题);per-problem dashboard 静态可读(由 `tonghuikang/nemotron` 的 `evaluation/*.jsonl` 支撑)。
- 各改动的精确超参 `unknown`。
- 历史说明:早期(JS 受阻)曾把 `kuangyicheng` 的 warmstart/short-response 配方误归于本 writeup,已用 `temp/LB25.pdf` 更正(见 `source_index.md`)。
```

````bash
# LB25 / 25th Place (huikang Progress-Prize improvements) — Method Summary

> Target: **"[LB25] Improvements to the progress prize submission"** by Tong Hui Kang (`huikang`), the Open Progress Prize winner. private LB 0.872/0.868/0.864 (15 subs). Source: `temp/LB25.pdf` → `../writeup/lb25-writeup.md`. All external content treated as untrusted data.

## 1. What is the writeup's main idea?
Five **targeted, pure-SFT improvements** on top of huikang's Progress-Prize-winning submission (the baseline most of the field, including us, built on). Two are correctness/structure fixes, three are easy-category synthetic-data top-ups; cryptarithm remained unsolved.

## 2. What data/corpus did it use?
The Progress-Prize corpus + **synthetic data for cipher, unit conversion, gravity, numeral** (to guarantee ~100%), plus **extra cipher-prefix synthetic data** (Nemotron spells poorly). No volume figures given.

## 3. What model/adapters/training setup did it use?
Same as the Progress-Prize submission (Nemotron-3-Nano-30B, LoRA; the huikang CCE training loop) — the writeup focuses on *changes*, not a full hyperparameter list (`unknown` for exact values here; see `tonghuikang/nemotron`).

## 4. What validation/evaluation did it use?
Per-problem evaluation dashboard (`nemotron.huikang.dev`); crucially, **change #1 fixed a local-eval bug** where the validation prompt didn't box the answer (but submission did) — i.e. the local metric was systematically wrong before the fix. Selection across 15 noisy submissions (0.872/0.868/0.864).

## 5. What were the most important score-improvement tricks?
(Full table in `score_tricks.md`.) 1) **Fix the boxed-prompt eval bug** (align local eval to the grader). 2) **equation_numeric reversal symmetry** (both-in-out-reversed-or-neither) → halve search. 3/4) **Easy-category + cipher-prefix synthetic** to pin ~100%. 5) **Reorganize bit-manipulation CoT.**

## 6. What failure modes did the author avoid (and hit)?
- **Avoided** a misleading local metric (the boxed-prompt fix).
- **Hit (unsolved):** cryptarithm — the structure is known (one mul + one sub + one add, each possibly ±1) but the trained LLM **devolves to repeating guesses**; no better-than-random guessing achieved.
- **Selection variance:** 0.872↔0.864 across 15 submissions — final selection under `temp=0` noise is itself a score determinant.

## 7. What makes this different from public 0.85/0.86 baselines and our attempts?
- LB25 **is** the baseline lineage (our v14 derives from huikang's Progress-Prize work). Its improvements are correctness/structure + easy-category polish, not a new hard-category method.
- vs **us**: the **boxed-prompt eval bug** mirrors our B4/T13 + INS-002 (local eval must match the grader exactly). The **equation reversal symmetry** is the earliest evidence (later confirmed by LB1/LB3/LB5/LB6/LB10/LB13) that equation has strong per-problem structure — i.e. **not a global cipher** (the 7th corroboration). cryptarithm unsolved even by the strongest baseline author confirms it's the top-end lever (LB1 catalog / LB3 two-stage). See `gap_analysis.md`.

| **Fix the boxed-prompt eval bug** | The validation prompt didn't box the answer (but submission did) → local eval systematically wrong; fixing it realigned validation with the LB. | change #1 | **High** (correct signal) | **Yes — = our B4/T13 + INS-002**; align local eval to grader exactly | Low |
| **equation_numeric reversal symmetry** | Either both inputs+outputs are reversed or neither (per problem) → halve the equation search. | change #2 | **Medium-High** | **Yes — re-check EQ premise** (earliest evidence equation has structure) | Low-Medium |
| **Easy-category synthetic (cipher/unit/gravity/numeral)** | Synthetic to guarantee ~100% on easy categories. | change #3 | **Medium** | **Yes** | Low |
| **Cipher-prefix synthetic (spelling)** | Nemotron spells poorly → synthetic data targeting cipher prefixes. | change #4 | **Medium** (cipher robustness) | **Yes** (cf. LB6 targeted subsets) | Low |
| **Reorganize bit-manipulation CoT** | Restructure the bit CoT. | change #5 | **Medium** (bit) | **Yes** (cf. LB1/5/6/10/13 bit redesigns) | Medium |
| **Submission selection under noise** | 0.872/0.868/0.864 across 15 subs — selection is a score determinant under temp=0 non-determinism. | §Result | **High (meta-lesson)** | **Yes** — trust LB aggregate; don't over-hedge (INS-002) | n/a |

## Provenance / attribution
- LB25 **is** the Progress-Prize baseline lineage by @huikang (`tonghuikang/nemotron`) that the field (and our v14) built on. These are *improvements on his own* submission.
- **Cross-writeup convergence:** the **equation reversal symmetry** here is the earliest of seven independent confirmations (LB1/LB3/LB5/LB6/LB10/LB13) that equation is per-problem-structured, **not a global cipher**; **cryptarithm unsolved** even by huikang confirms it as the top-end lever (LB1 signature catalog / LB3 two-stage).
EOF
````

```
NVIDIA Nemotron Model Reasoning Challenge
Solution Writeup · 88th place · Jun 16, 2026

92th PLACE SOLUTION
Introduction and Acknowledgements

First, we would like to sincerely thank the organizers for hosting this competition, the Kaggle
community for sharing valuable discussions and notebooks, and our teammates for working
through the competition together. We learned from many shared insights and were able to enjoy
the process until the end.

Solution Overview

Our solution was based on End-to-end finetuning for LB 0.85 and was also heavily influenced by
the following public notebooks. We would like to thank the authors again.

   •   Training with Unsloth to Achieve 0.85 LB
   •   End-to-end finetuning for LB 0.85
   •   Tinker submission notebook

Our approach can be summarized in the following three points.

We made almost no changes to the reasoner (CoT generation logic)

   •   The reasoner was based on Open Progress Prize Publication, and we made almost no
       changes to it.
   •   The reasoner could correctly solve 87.8% of the problems, while the best score from the
       public notebooks was 0.86. Therefore, we believed that if the LLM could reproduce the
       behavior of the reasoner more faithfully, a high ranking would be achievable.
   •   Our approach was not to solve harder problems, but to avoid losing problems that should
       already be solvable.
   •   Below is the final accuracy of our reasoner. It is almost the same as the publicly
       available one.

         Category       Found Total Accuracy Avg ms
bit_manipulation        1364 1602 85.1%      0.8
cipher                  1576 1576 100.0% 0.1
cryptarithm_deduce      59    659 9.0%       0.0
cryptarithm_guess       13    164 7.9%       0.0
equation_numeric_deduce 541 596 90.8%        0.6
equation_numeric_guess 21     136 15.4%      0.6
       Category           Found Total Accuracy Avg ms
gravity                   1597 1597 100.0% 0.1
numeral                   1576 1576 100.0% 0.0
unit_conversion           1594 1594 100.0% 0.0
TOTAL                     8341 9500 87.8%      0.2

We built a new generator and synthesized many similar problems

   •   Although the reasoner could correctly solve 87.8% of the problems, the best public
       notebook score remained at 0.86. We suspected that the gap was caused by a shortage of
       training data.
   •   Therefore, we extracted various task-level statistics from train.csv and built a program
       that could generate an arbitrary number of rule_found samples.
   •   The statistics we used included character frequencies, numeric ranges and distributions,
       and distributions of transformation methods.
   •   To improve the quality of the generator, we trained the model only on synthetic data and
       evaluated it on both synthetic data and original data. If the synthetic data perfectly
       imitated the original data, the evaluation accuracy on synthetic data and original data
       should be the same. By measuring this gap, we identified missing factors in the synthetic
       data generation algorithm and iteratively fixed them.
•   In the final submission, we trained with a ratio of "synthetic data : original data = 2.5 : 1",
    using synthetic data first and then original data.
•   Longer training improved the loss, especially on difficult tasks.
Tokenization trick (synthetic tokens for cryptarithm)

   •   In cryptarithm tasks, tokenizer segmentation sometimes caused multiple characters to be
       handled as a single token. This issue was also discussed in the competition discussions.
   •   To address this, we used synthetic tokens that force each single character to be encoded
       as one token, making the learning process more stable.
Additional Improvements

Gradient clipping

   •   In the public notebook, the gradient clipping value was set extremely high at 1e9.
   •   We found that this was causing training instability, so we clipped gradients at 1.5.
   •   There were discussions about scores varying from submission to submission, and we
       believe this may have been one of the causes.
   •   The figure below shows an example where the same training setup produced very
       different LB scores depending on whether gradient explosion occurred.
Local validation strategy

   •   Until the middle of the competition, we validated by training on synthetic data and
       evaluating on original data. For submissions, we trained on both synthetic data and
       original data.
   •   However, as we improved the quality of the generator, the model became increasingly
       overfit to the original data, and we observed a divergence between local validation and
       Public LB.
   •   Therefore, for the final stage, we decided to prioritize Public LB, which was based on
       unseen data, over local validation.

What Did Not Work

Generating CoTs with higher temperature and applying reinforcement learning (SimPO /
ORPO)
   •   When we inspected model failures, we found that in many cases the model produced
       CoTs that were very close to the correct ones. Therefore, we thought that instead of only
       increasing the probability of correct outputs through SFT, we also needed to reduce the
       probability of failures through reinforcement learning.
   •   To create failed examples (rejected), we sampled from the SFT model with temperature
       set to 1.3.
   •   For chosen, we used the output of the reasoner as is.
   •   We performed preference learning with SimPO / ORPO using these output pairs.
       However, it did not improve accuracy as much as expected, so we did not use it in the
       final submission.
   •   In the training logs, we observed some cases where the probability of the chosen side
       increased, but we saw almost no decrease in the probability of the rejected side, which
       was what we had expected.
   •   We believe that learning did not progress sufficiently because chosen and rejected
       were too similar.




Solving new problems

   •   For us, solving bit_manipulation and cryptarithm tasks and creating CoTs that an LLM
       could imitate was very difficult.
   •   Algorithms that solve these problems with high accuracy require a large amount of
       search, and it was very difficult for an LLM to imitate them within a limited token
       budget.
   •   We also used Claude Fable 5, but we were not able to develop a sufficiently strong
       reasoner.
```

```markdown
## Introduction & acknowledgements
Thanks to the organizers and community. Built on **"End-to-end finetuning for LB 0.85"**, heavily influenced by public notebooks: **"Training with Unsloth to Achieve 0.85 LB"**, **"End-to-end finetuning for LB 0.85"**, **"Tinker submission notebook"**.

## Solution overview — three points

### 1. Almost no changes to the reasoner (CoT generation logic)
- The reasoner was based on the **Open Progress Prize Publication** (@huikang); almost unchanged.
- It correctly solves **87.8%** of train problems, while the best public-notebook LB was 0.86. So the bet: if the LLM **reproduces the reasoner more faithfully**, a high rank is achievable.
- **Philosophy: not to solve harder problems, but to avoid losing problems that should already be solvable.**

Reasoner oracle (≈ the public one):

| Category | Found | Total | Accuracy |
|---|---|---|---|
| bit_manipulation | 1364 | 1602 | 85.1% |
| cipher | 1576 | 1576 | 100.0% |
| cryptarithm_deduce | 59 | 659 | 9.0% |
| cryptarithm_guess | 13 | 164 | 7.9% |
| equation_numeric_deduce | 541 | 596 | 90.8% |
| equation_numeric_guess | 21 | 136 | 15.4% |
| gravity | 1597 | 1597 | 100.0% |
| numeral | 1576 | 1576 | 100.0% |
| unit_conversion | 1594 | 1594 | 100.0% |
| **TOTAL** | **8341** | **9500** | **87.8%** |

### 2. New generator → synthesize many similar problems
- Reasoner solves 87.8% but the best public LB stayed at 0.86 → suspected a **training-data shortage**.
- Extracted **task-level statistics from train.csv** (character frequencies, numeric ranges/distributions, distributions of transformation methods) and built a generator for **arbitrary `rule_found` samples**.
- **Generator-quality QC loop:** train **only on synthetic**, evaluate on **both synthetic and original**; if the synthetic perfectly imitated the original, the two accuracies would match. **The gap reveals missing factors** in the generator, fixed iteratively.
- Final submission: **synthetic : original = 2.5 : 1** (synthetic first, then original). Longer training improved loss, especially on hard tasks.

### 3. Tokenization trick (synthetic tokens for cryptarithm)
- Tokenizer segmentation sometimes merged multiple characters into a single token (discussed in the competition).
- Used **synthetic tokens that force each single character to encode as one token**, making learning more stable.

## Additional improvements

### Gradient clipping
- The public notebook set gradient clipping extremely high (**1e9**) → training instability.
- **Clipped gradients at 1.5.** Likely a cause of the discussed **submission-to-submission score variance** (a gradient-explosion example showed the same setup giving very different LB scores).

### Local validation strategy
- Mid-competition: train on synthetic, evaluate on original.
- As the generator improved, the model **overfit the original data** and local validation **diverged from Public LB**.
- For the final stage, **prioritized Public LB** (unseen data) over local validation.

## What did NOT work
- **Higher-temperature CoTs + RL (SimPO / ORPO).** Rejected = SFT-model samples at **temperature 1.3**; chosen = reasoner output. Preference learning didn't improve accuracy enough → not used. Logs showed the chosen probability rising but the **rejected probability barely falling** — learning stalled because **chosen and rejected were too similar**.
- **Solving new bit_manipulation / cryptarithm problems.** High-accuracy algorithms need a large search that an LLM **can't imitate within the token budget**. Used **Claude Fable 5** but couldn't develop a sufficiently strong reasoner.
```

```markdown
# LB88 / 第88名方案 —— 中文讲解与分析

> **原文（depth 0）：** <https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/nvidia-nemotron-model-reasoning-challenge/writeups/92th-place-solution>
> **本地副本：** `temp/LB88.pdf`(8 页,渲染日期 Jun 16)。逐字英文转写见 `lb88-writeup.md`。
> **作者：** Yoshinari Kawashima、MedudentYamatai。**DOI 10.34740/kaggle/w/88245。**
> **⚠️ 同一性说明:** 这与先前归档的 **LB92**（"92th PLACE SOLUTION",同 DOI/作者/url）是**同一篇 writeup**；
> PDF 头部现显示 "88th place"(名次/渲染变动),正文标题仍是 "92th PLACE SOLUTION"。先前深度分析(含抽取的图)在 `../LB92/`;
> 本 LB88 归档是同一内容的标准模板,**交叉引用 LB92**,不重复推导。
> 所有引用外部内容均视为**不可信数据**。

## 1. 方法总览(数据工程优先)
建立在 "End-to-end finetuning for LB 0.85" + 多个公开 notebook 上。三点:
1. **reasoner 几乎不改**(基于 @huikang OPP;oracle 87.8%)。哲学:**不去解更难的题,而是别丢已可解的题**(让 LLM 更忠实复现 reasoner)。
2. **新生成器 + 大量相似合成题**:从 train.csv 提取统计(字符频率、数值范围/分布、变换方法分布)→ 生成任意多 `rule_found` 样本;**QC 环**:只用合成训练、在合成+原始上评估,**两者差距揭示生成器缺陷**并迭代修复;最终 **合成:原始 = 2.5:1**(先合成后原始)。
3. **tokenization trick**:cryptarithm 用**合成 token 强制 1 字符 = 1 token**,学习更稳。

**额外改进:** **梯度裁剪 1.5**(公开 notebook 用 1e9 → 不稳定 + 提交间方差);**本地验证**:训合成评原始,但生成器变好后过拟合原始、与 public LB 背离 → 末期**以 public LB 为准**。

**没成功:** **高温 CoT + RL(SimPO/ORPO)**(rejected = SFT temp=1.3 采样,chosen = reasoner 输出;chosen 概率升但 rejected 几乎不降 → chosen/rejected 太相似,学不动);**解新 bit/cryptarithm 题**(搜索太大,LLM token 预算内学不会;用了 Claude Fable 5 也没造出够强的 reasoner)。

oracle:bit 85.1%、cipher/trivial 100%、cryptarithm ~9%、equation_deduce 90.8%、equation_guess 15.4%;总 87.8%。

## 2. 对我们可复用(详见 `../LB92/` 的先前分析)

| 技巧 | 可复用 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| **统计匹配合成 + 合成-vs-原始 gap QC 环** | ✅ 高价值 | 精化我方"合成稀释":朴素 synth 稀释,**统计匹配 + gap 验证 + 2.5:1** 能迁移。 |
| **逐字符 tokenization(符号类)** | ✅ 新、未试 | 直击我方 equation/cipher/cryptarithm 弱点的 BPE 合并问题。 |
| **梯度裁剪 1.5**(我方用 1e9-off) | ✅ 治提交间方差 | 便宜 A/B。 |
| **保护已可解题(别丢)** 哲学 | ✅ = 我方 T12 抗稀释 | 不去解更难,先别回退。 |
| **末期以 public/unseen 为准**(生成器变好后本地过拟合) | ⚠️ 张力 | 与 LB3/LB5/LB6/LB10"按 private/validation 选模"相反 —— LB88 的本地是"训合成评原始",过拟合原始后失真;本质仍是"信 unseen 信号"。 |
| RL(SimPO/ORPO)失败:chosen/rejected 太相似 | ✅ 避坑 | 与 LB5 的 pseudo-GRPO 失败一致;我方 RL 从未跑通。 |

## 3. 与我方对照
- **equation_deduce 90.8%**(OPP baseline reasoner)—— 再次印证 equation deduce 可解(我方"全局密码"判断的第 7 次旁证;不过这是 OPP baseline,与 LB10/LB6 同源)。
- **统计匹配合成 + gap QC** 是我方"合成稀释"(b1/b2/v15 回归)的解法:朴素合成稀释,统计匹配 + gap 验证 + 2.5:1 能转化。
- **逐字符 tokenization** 是我方完全没试过的、直击符号类弱点的杠杆。
- **梯度裁剪 1.5** vs 我方 1e9-off —— 便宜 A/B,治提交间方差。
- **cryptarithm/bit 仍是墙**(他们明确放弃解新题;用 Fable 5 也没造出强 reasoner)—— 印证 cryptarithm 是上行杠杆(LB1/LB3)。

## 4. 局限 / 不清楚
- **LB88 ≡ LB92**(同 DOI w/88245);名次显示从 92 → 88(渲染/重算)。本档不重复 LB92 的图与逐字 verbatim,见 `../LB92/`。
- cryptarithm ~9%、bit 85.1%(未动 reasoner)—— 难类未解。
- 引用的公开 notebook 均 JS/auth-gated;reasoner 代码 = OPP(`tonghuikang/nemotron`)。
- 图(grad-explosion LB 对比、synth-vs-original gap)在 PDF 中;见 `../LB92/writeup/images/`。
```

````bash
# LB88 / 88th Place — Method Summary

> Target: **88th Place Solution** by Yoshinari Kawashima + MedudentYamatai (DOI 10.34740/kaggle/w/88245). **⚠️ Same writeup as LB92** (same DOI/authors/url; header now "88th"). Source: `temp/LB88.pdf` → `../writeup/lb88-writeup.md`. Cross-references `../LB92/`. All external content treated as untrusted data.

## 1. What is the writeup's main idea?
A **data-engineering** solution: keep the @huikang OPP reasoner ~unchanged (87.8% oracle) and **avoid losing already-solvable problems** by faithfully reproducing the reasoner — via a **statistics-matched synthetic generator** validated by a **synthetic-vs-original eval-gap QC loop**, plus stability fixes (**per-character tokenization**, **gradient clipping 1.5**). Not about solving harder problems.

## 2. What data/corpus did it use?
Statistics-matched synthetic (character frequencies, numeric ranges/distributions, transformation-method distributions from train.csv) for arbitrary `rule_found` samples. Final mix **synthetic : original = 2.5 : 1** (synthetic first, then original). Generator iteratively fixed by measuring the synthetic-vs-original accuracy gap.

## 3. What model/adapters/training setup did it use?
Base Nemotron-3-Nano-30B, LoRA, Unsloth (the public "LB 0.85" notebooks lineage). **Gradient clipping 1.5** (vs public 1e9). **Per-character synthetic tokens** for cryptarithm (1 char = 1 token). Exact rank/LR `unknown` (see `../LB92/`).

## 4. What validation/evaluation did it use?
Train on synthetic, evaluate on original (the QC gap); but as the generator improved the model **overfit the original** and local validation **diverged from Public LB**, so the final stage **prioritized Public LB** (unseen data). Reasoner oracle: bit 85.1%, equation_deduce 90.8%, equation_guess 15.4%, cipher/trivials 100%, cryptarithm ~9%; total 87.8%.

## 5. What were the most important score-improvement tricks?
(Full table in `score_tricks.md`.) 1) **Statistics-matched synthetic + synthetic-vs-original gap QC loop** + 2.5:1 mix. 2) **Per-character tokenization** for symbol categories (cryptarithm BPE-merge fix). 3) **Gradient clipping 1.5** (fixes instability / submission variance from the public 1e9). 4) **"Don't lose solvable problems"** framing + longer training on hard tasks.

## 6. What failure modes did the author avoid (and hit)?
- **Avoided** gradient-explosion instability (clip 1.5) and BPE token-merge on symbols (per-char tokens).
- **Hit:** RL (SimPO/ORPO) didn't help — chosen (reasoner) and rejected (temp-1.3 samples) **too similar**; couldn't build a strong new bit/cryptarithm reasoner (search too big for the token budget), even with Claude Fable 5.

## 7. What makes this different from public 0.85/0.86 baselines and our attempts?
- A pure **coverage/stability** play (don't regress) rather than a new hard-category method.
- vs **us**: the **statistics-matched + gap-validated synthetic** is the antidote to our "synthetic dilutes" (b1/b2/v15 regressed); **per-character tokenization** is a novel, untried lever on our symbol weak spot; **grad-clip 1.5** vs our 1e9-off is a cheap A/B for submission variance. equation_deduce 90.8% (OPP baseline) corroborates the equation-is-solvable finding. cryptarithm/bit unchanged (~9%/85%). See `gap_analysis.md` and `../LB92/analysis/`.
EOF

| **Gradient clipping 1.5** | Public used 1e9 → instability / submission variance; clip at 1.5. | §Additional | **Medium** (variance) | **Yes — cheap A/B vs our 1e9-off** | Low |
| **"Don't lose solvable problems" framing** | Optimize faithful reproduction of an 87.8% reasoner, not harder problems. | §Overview 1 | **Medium (framing)** | **Yes — = our T12 anti-dilution** | n/a |
| **Longer training on hard tasks** | Longer training improved loss, esp. hard tasks. | §Overview 2 | **Low-Medium** | **Yes** | Low |
| **RL (SimPO/ORPO)** (negative) | chosen=reasoner, rejected=temp-1.3 samples; chosen prob rose but rejected barely fell (too similar) → dropped. | §What didn't work | **Negative** | **Avoid** (cf. LB5 pseudo-GRPO) | High |
| **Solving new bit/cryptarithm** (negative) | Search too big for the LLM token budget; Claude Fable 5 couldn't build a strong reasoner. | §What didn't work | **Negative** | Use LB1/LB3 structure instead | High |

## Provenance / attribution
- Built on **"End-to-end finetuning for LB 0.85"** + public 0.85 notebooks + **@huikang OPP reasoner** (unchanged).
- **Novel:** statistics-matched-synthetic + gap QC, per-character tokenization, grad-clip 1.5. (Same as LB92.)
- **Cross-writeup convergence:** RL fails here (SimPO/ORPO) and in LB5 (pseudo-GRPO) — chosen/rejected too similar; cryptarithm/bit "wall" they chose not to attack (cf. LB5/LB6/LB10/LB13).
EOF

cat > analysis/gap_analysis.md <<'EOF'
# LB88 / 88th Place — Gap analysis (us vs the 88th-place writeup)

> **Same writeup as LB92** — this is a condensed gap analysis; the fuller prior pass is `../LB92/analysis/gap_analysis.md`.
> "our approach" cites `competitions/nvidia-nemotron/{notes,submissions,equation-frontier,bugs}.md`. "writeup" cites `../writeup/lb88-writeup.md`.

| area | our approach | writeup approach | gap | lesson |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| corpus construction | huikang corpus + small synth (diluted). (submissions.md:31) | Statistics-matched synthetic, 2.5:1 synth:original, gap-QC'd. | Ours diluting; theirs matched + validated | Match train statistics; validate the synth-vs-original gap |
| reasoning traces | bit 10%, equation 0.4% coverage. (notes.md:72-73) | OPP reasoner unchanged (87.8%); focus on faithful reproduction. | We change the recipe; they protect the reasoner | "Don't lose solvable problems" |
| synthetic data | b1/b2/v15 regressed. (submissions.md:31) | Statistics-matched + gap QC + 2.5:1 → transfers. | The exact fix for our dilution | Statistics-matched, gap-validated synth can help |
| cryptarithm / bit | ~10% / ~90% unsolved. (bugs.md:14, notes.md:73) | ~9% / 85.1% (reasoner unchanged; chose not to attack). | Both weak | cryptarithm/bit is the wall (LB1/LB3 needed) |
| equation | global cipher (EQ-0/EQ-2′). (equation-frontier.md:209-228) | equation_deduce 90.8% (OPP baseline). | Premise corroboration (7th) | equation deduce solvable |
| tokenization | default BPE. (notes.md) | **Per-character synthetic tokens** for symbols. | We never tried per-char | Novel lever on our symbol weak spot |
| training stability | grad-clip 1e9-off. (notes.md) | **grad-clip 1.5**. | Cheap A/B | Tame submission variance |
| validation | T12 late; trust LB aggregate. (submissions.md:76-78) | train-synth/eval-original; overfit → prioritize Public LB late. | Both end at "trust unseen LB" | A train-derived metric overfits as the generator improves |
| RL | never ran. (notes.md:107) | SimPO/ORPO failed (chosen≈rejected). | RL didn't pay off | Skip RL here (cf. LB5) |
| merge | soup +0.01. (insights.md:44) | no merge. | — | — |

## Why our attempts didn't close the gap
- **synthetic (b1/b2/v15):** diluting; LB88's **statistics-matched + gap-QC + 2.5:1** is the fix.
- **equation:** equation_deduce 90.8% — 7th corroboration that deduce is solvable (re-test, no GPU).
- **tokenization:** we never tried **per-character tokens** for symbols — a concrete untried lever.
- **stability:** our 1e9-off grad clip may cause submission variance; A/B clip 1.5.

## High-value vs not-worth-it
**High value:** statistics-matched synthetic + synth-vs-original gap QC + 2.5:1; **per-character tokenization** for symbols; **grad-clip 1.5**; protect already-solvable categories.
**Not worth:** RL (SimPO/ORPO — chosen≈rejected); attacking new bit/cryptarithm without LB1/LB3 structure.
EOF

cat > analysis/next_version_plan.md <<'EOF'
# Next-version plan — `lb88-v1`

> Derived from the **88th Place Solution** (= LB92; see `../LB92/analysis/next_version_plan.md` for the prior `v18-stable` plan).
> **Status: PLAN ONLY.** No GPU training, submit, kernel push, or dataset upload (`allow_* = false`; comp ended).

## Version name
`lb88-v1` (≈ LB92's `v18-stable`)

## Hypothesis
Our "synthetic dilutes" failure is fixable with **statistics-matched synthetic + a synthetic-vs-original gap QC loop** (final ~2.5:1), and symbol-category learning is unblocked by **per-character tokenization**; **grad-clip 1.5** tames submission variance. None require solving cryptarithm/bit harder.

## What we borrow from LB88/LB92
- Statistics-matched generator (char freq, numeric ranges, transform distributions) + **synthetic-vs-original eval-gap QC** to iteratively fix the generator; ramp toward **2.5:1 synth:original** only if QC + hard-val hold.
- **Per-character tokenization** (synthetic tokens) for equation/cipher/cryptarithm.
- **Gradient clipping 1.5** (A/B vs our 1e9-off; watch run-to-run variance).
- **Protect already-solvable categories** (= our T12 anti-dilution).

## What new ideas we add
- Combine with LB1/LB3 cryptarithm structure (LB88 deliberately didn't attack it).
- Equation-deduce re-crack (no GPU) — shared with `lb{1,3,5,6,10,13}-v1`.

## Data / corpus, training, validation
- Statistics-matched synth + gap QC; per-char tokens; grad-clip 1.5; Unsloth/CCE. Validate with **category-stratified + hard-val** scored by the official extractor; gate on T12 ≥ 0.764 + no easy-cat regression. Down-scaled RTX Pro 6000 run ≈ 6-12h to validate the mechanism.

## Submit / no-submit gate, risks, rollback
- Comp over → gate N/A. Risks: per-char tokens may interact with the base tokenizer; grad-clip A/B confounded by other changes; generator fidelity. **Hold-best = soup (0.86/0.85) + eq-aug (0.86/0.86); revert on regression.** All on a branch / under `runs/`; no held-best overwrite; no force-push.

## Implementation checklist
- [ ] No-GPU: equation-deduce re-crack (shared).
- [ ] Statistics-matched generator + synthetic-vs-original gap QC.
- [ ] Per-character tokenization for symbol categories.
- [ ] grad-clip 1.5 A/B (variance check).
- [ ] (GPU-gated) down-scaled run; T12 + category-stratified eval; no easy-cat regression.

(Full detail in `../LB92/analysis/next_version_plan.md`.)
EOF

cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# LB88 / 88th Place Solution — post-competition archive

Post-competition archive for the **88th Place Solution** by **Yoshinari Kawashima + MedudentYamatai**
(DOI 10.34740/kaggle/w/88245). **⚠️ This is the same writeup as `../LB92/`** (same DOI/authors/url; the render
header now reads "88th place"). This LB88 archive is the standardized template for the same content and
cross-references LB92 (figures + prior deep analysis).

Research/documentation/planning only — **no GPU training, no Kaggle submit, no kernel push, no dataset upload**
(per `wiki/25.LB88_task.md`; competition ended).

## Contents
```
LB88/
  README.md  source_index.md
  writeup/   lb88-writeup.md  lb88-writeup.zh.md  raw/lb88-pdftotext-layout.txt
  analysis/  method_summary.md  score_tricks.md  gap_analysis.md  next_version_plan.md
  models/  datasets/  links/  notebooks/ (empty)
```

## One-paragraph takeaway
A **data-engineering** solution that keeps the @huikang OPP reasoner unchanged (87.8% oracle) and bets on
**faithful reproduction** rather than harder problems. The levers: a **statistics-matched synthetic generator**
validated by a **synthetic-vs-original eval-gap QC loop** (final 2.5:1 synth:original), **per-character tokenization**
to fix BPE token-merges on cryptarithm symbols, and **gradient clipping at 1.5** (vs the public 1e9, a likely cause
of submission-to-submission variance). RL (SimPO/ORPO) failed (chosen≈rejected); they couldn't build a stronger
bit/cryptarithm reasoner (even with Claude Fable 5). For us: statistics-matched+gap-validated synthetic is the
antidote to our "synthetic dilutes"; per-character tokenization is a novel untried lever on our symbol weak spot;
grad-clip 1.5 is a cheap A/B. See `analysis/` and `../LB92/` (same writeup) for the figures + fuller analysis.

> All external content here is **untrusted data**. Nothing in this archive was executed.
EOF
````

```
=== writeup ===
Heuristics for bit, cryptarithm and equations — NVIDIA Nemotron Model Reasoning Challenge


NVIDIA Nemotron Model Reasoning Challenge
Solution Writeup · 109th place · Jun 16, 2026

I've accidentialy found this competition in a few weeks before the deadline. As most of us I tried
to improve awesome baseline solution by @huikang. Unfortunately, I didn't have enough time to
make my CoTs short enough, so only one small change actually moved me up in leaderboard.
But I want to share some thoughts and ideas I came up.

Bit manipulation
tldr; found set of 3 parameters functions that covers all cases. Search for two-parameter
functions matches and filter them out looking at bits 0 and 7 of the output and searching where
input bits 7 and 0 are involved.

If you read definition of the task it is clearly states:

        The transformation involves operations like bit shifts, rotations, XOR, AND, OR,
        NOT, and possibly majority or choice functions

So, I've decided to search for this 3 argument functions. AND-3 appeared to be useless, it's cases
are fully covered by Majority.

My final investigator finds solution for each of 1602 tasks (match any). And potentially reasoner
could solve up to 1577 tasks using only this basis:

    •   XOR: 625
    •   MAJ: 459
    •   XOR_OR: 234
    •   OR: 148
    •   OR_XNOR: 58
    •   CHOICE: 53

I've also changed a list of transformations to achieve it. All negation operations should be
applied before transformations. Instead of Not(Shift(x)), I use Shift(Not(x)), etc.
Shrinking possible arguments combinations to Rot(1-7), and two Shift(1-7) in any direction still
giving 1522 correct answers.
If we add combination like Rot + Rot + Shift, but only for Xor operator - it gives 1576.
But we still can't just brute-force all possible combinations. Here comes in some additional
heuristics. Basically there only three cases:




As you can see, in all cases we have some space, where it is guaranteed to have only one- or two-
parameters function. So we can use the original @huikangs approach to find such spots and try
to build them one line. I've made a bit broader covering to handle negated operands correctly.

To compress the CoT for additional operators I build also negated-output matching table. It gives
e.g. if one of AND candidates matched to the negative one, then it is by the De Morgan's low
Not(A and B) -> Not(A) or Not(B)

After that we have a few groups:

g_xor = XOR, XOR-NOT
g_or = OR, OR-NOT, NOT-OR, NOT-OR-NOT
g_and = AND, AND-NOT, NOT-AND, NOT-AND-NOT
g_iden = Identity, NOT
content_copy

1) Two left-shifts or two right-shifts

In this case we check what happens on side and what is in the middle.

 Side Middle     Candidate function
g_iden gxor XOR3, OR_XNOR, XOR_OR
g_iden g_or OR3, XOR_OR
g_iden g_and OR_XNOR, CHOICE
g_iden g_iden CHOICE
 Side Middle    Candidate function
C0    g_and MAJ

After that we have a lot of candidates and we try to filter-out as much as possible before final
brute-force. There are two branches: LShift and RShift but they are quite symmetric.

Lets take a look at LShift+LShift+Rot case in the picture:




We will have at least one identity match on the right side.
Using the Identity candidate (index 2 in this case), we can calculate rotation LRot(3) and find the
first spot spot to the left, where two parameter function matches. We are looking only for
candidates who has 7 as one of indexes (0 for right shift) and match selected rotation in the same
position.
If it is not found - we check the next one. In this picture the perfect candidate would have match
to 7-7 and three Identity matches in a row to the right of it.

Now we have a few pairs of ROT(const)+LShift(const)+LShift(x) - the last one we can just
brute-force. But as heuristic we can use the fact, that we must see some amount of two operands
operations matches in a row. So as the first candidate we should use the spot where it ends (in
picture 7-6-6).

My problem was here mostly with C0 candidates or AND operations, because they give too
much candidates when the output columns are like "000000"

2,3 Left shift + Right shift

This case is easier. You guaranted to see on the both sides some matches. In most cases you can
easily calculate the Rotation candidate.
In case (2) a good pair from both sides selected, where on of indexes is X for the left side and X-1
mod 8 for the right.
E.g. AND33, XOR26 -> LRot(3), LShift(3), RShift(1).
Then we calculate where they should overlap and check if the sequence for each function
continues till that point:




For left-right I also have a table of candidate functions, but now they are divided by sides:

 Left Rght Candidate function
g_xor g_xor XOR3, OR_XNOR
g_or g_or OR3, XOR_OR
g_and g_and MAJ, CHOICE
 Left Rght Candidate function
g_xor g_or XOR_OR
g_and g_xor OR_XNOR
g_and g_iden CHOICE
g_and C0     Maj

For the case (3) we can also check the middle for Identity/Constant matches that should be in
between of shifts.

2 Rotation + Shift




Additional ~50 tasks could be solved if we check such cases with XOR function. And it is quite
easy to do actually. Lets take a look at XOR-3 ANF:

XOR(A,B,C) = A ⊕ B ⊕ C; then XOR(A,B,C) ⊕ C = A ⊕ B ⊕ C ⊕ C = A ⊕ B

We have a list of all possible XOR(A,B) and Output is XOR(A,B,C). The only thing we have to
do is to build list of possible XOR(Output, C) and match it on the XOR(A,B) table.

Why it all didn't work

My mistake was, that I've spend too much time trying to reach a perfect solution. I could apply
e.g. only the XOR3 heuristic, it would already give me some small boost..
I've implemented everything above, but there were a lot of cases where final brute-force is too
big and I didn't have enough time how to compress it. I think the good enough solution would be
to score each potential candidate by length and how much info does it gives. Most of bad cases
were output columns with 00000 or 111111.

Another approach

I also had another approach in mind that I didn't have time to try. It is the same trick as for XOR
function. We can write down ANFs for all functions, partially calculate them and then XOR it on
the output:

OR(x,y,z)=x⊕y⊕z⊕xy⊕xz⊕yz⊕xyz

XOR_OR(x,y,z)=x⊕y⊕z⊕xz⊕yz
Choice(x,y,z)=z⊕xy⊕xz

Maj(x,y,z)=xy⊕xz⊕yz

XOR(x,y,z)=x⊕y⊕z

OR_XNOR(x,y,z)=1⊕x⊕y⊕z⊕xy

The xyz is a bit problematic, but it could be resolved for only appropriate candidates on the
edges. Same approach - we make XOR on Output and match on one of pre-calculated tables. I
think this one was really perspective…

Cryptarythm
For cryptarythm it was important to understand the restrictions of the dataset itself. It is possible
to correctly determine the right class of operators in 781 cases out of 823 in total if restrict the
operations by following classes:

Concatenation -> concat, reverse concat, big\little-endian

Multiplication -> mul + offset{-1,0,1}

Summation -> sum + offset{-1,0,1}

Substraction -> absdiff, signed substraction, negative absdiff, right-left substraction

How to map them? In most cases the meaning is the same as symbols semantic. Like * is mul, +
is sum, etc.
But sometime we don't have appropriate symbols. And also sometimes the original symbols
change meaning. We can check such cases by simple rules:

   •   check for concats first (+ and * are also quite often concats)
   •   If we don't have *,-,+ we look at right side size (4 -> mul, 1 -> sub, 2-> sum\sub, 3 ->
       sum\mul).
   •   for *,-,+ apply by their meaning if there are no contradictions
   •   If some of the operations are taken, then use another one for yours
   •   if operator is only in question (guess tasks) - use unused operation. If there multiple - use
       opposite to the presented one. E.g. * is substraction from exaples, then / in question is
       summation, etc.

This list is not full, but you got the idea - even for the guess questions there are some deduction
steps how to find good candidate for the operation.
Full determenistic search gives 751 right answers in such constraints.

After that I build mappings and write down equations with offsets and substraction branching
included for big and little endian. Something like this:
Big-endian mapped formulas:
E1: 10*A+B+10*C+D+m=100*E+10*C+E # m is offset for multiplication
E2: (10*F+E)*(10*B+D)+l=1000*E+100*A+10*D+D # l is offset for summation
E3: 10*G+D+10*G+H+m=100*E+10*I+I
content_copy

After that I build mod 10 restrictions. It cut many branches early:

Big-endian mod 10 constraints:
Use full equations modulo 10 before decimal columns.
M1: B+D+m=1 (mod 10)
M2: D+l=D (mod 10)
M3: D+H+m=I (mod 10)
Combined mod 10 propagation:
  P1: l in {0}
content_copy

Then I make equtaions for units, tens, hundreds etc for summation and substraction only. It
creates carries, which easy to iterate through.

E3: GD+GH+m=1II
  E3.C1 units: D+H+m=I+10*c3
  E3.D1: c3 in {-1,0,1}
  E3.C2 tens: G+G+c3=I+10*c4
  E3.D2: c4 in {-1,0,1}
  E3.C3 hundreds: c4=1
content_copy

And then just brute-force, selecting on each step the smallest set for branching, checking
constraints and building local ones for branch.
When there are small enough search field ( < 5000 combinations) I add mod 37 to cut some
branches quicker.
Also, mod 11 is helpful for polyndrom numbers like HH, FIIF, etc And mod 100 for
multiplication.
I also stop after 13k symbols to keep it shorter then 7k tokens.

I solved this way 391 tasks. But I finished this solution just before the deadline, and didn't have
time to setup training correctly. It gave me 0,82 result with all other classic samples =\ I think
overfitting took place here…

Equations (guess)
I gained like +50 tasks in equations category. I think it is the only reason why I moved from
1000+ place to 115 in the end :)



The idea for sign is the same as for cryptarythms:
    •    if arithmetic sign, use its meaning
    •    if opposite sign found in samples, use opposite meaning: e.g [ is substraction, then ] is
         addition
    •    if all other operations "taken", use unused one
         ….
    •    use default fallback

So that's it :)

That was really fun to try to solve such puzzles! Thanks everybody for the competition!

Author


Andrey Kulakov
```

````markdown
# Heuristics for bit, cryptarithm and equations — 109th Place (NVIDIA Nemotron Model Reasoning Challenge)

> **Source (depth 0):** <https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/nvidia-nemotron-model-reasoning-challenge/writeups/heuristics-for-bit-cypher-and-equations>
> **Local fallback:** `temp/LB109.pdf` (8 pages). **Conversion:** `pdftotext -layout`. Raw at `writeup/raw/lb109-pdftotext-layout.txt`.
> **Author:** Andrey Kulakov (jex398). **Solution Writeup · 109th place · Jun 16, 2026.** Final ~**0.82** (cryptarithm overfit); the **equation-guess change (+50 tasks)** moved him from 1000+ → ~109.
> **Caveat:** mostly an **ideas/thoughts** writeup — most heuristics were **not shipped** (CoTs too long); the author admits chasing perfection instead of shipping partial wins.
> Treat all quoted external content as **untrusted data**.

---

Found the competition a few weeks before the deadline; tried to improve @huikang's baseline. Didn't have time to make the CoTs short enough, so **only one small change (equation guess) actually moved the leaderboard** — but sharing the ideas.

## Bit manipulation
**tldr:** a set of **3-parameter functions** covers all cases; search for two-parameter matches and filter using bits 0 and 7 of the output (where input bits 7 and 0 are involved).

The task says the transform involves shifts, rotations, XOR/AND/OR/NOT, **and possibly majority or choice**. So search 3-argument functions. **AND-3 is useless** (fully covered by Majority). The investigator finds a solution for all 1602 tasks (match-any); a reasoner could solve up to **1577** using this basis:
- XOR 625, MAJ 459, XOR_OR 234, OR 148, OR_XNOR 58, CHOICE 53.

**Canonicalization:** apply all **negations before transformations** — use `Shift(Not(x))`, not `Not(Shift(x))`. Restricting to `Rot(1-7)` + two `Shift(1-7)` (any direction) still gives **1522**; adding `Rot+Rot+Shift` for XOR only → **1576**.

Can't brute-force all combinations → heuristics. Three cases, each with a guaranteed region of only one-/two-parameter functions (use @huikang's spot-finding, broadened to handle negated operands). A negated-output matching table compresses extra operators via **De Morgan** (`Not(A and B) → Not(A) or Not(B)`). Groups:
```
g_xor  = XOR, XOR-NOT
g_or   = OR, OR-NOT, NOT-OR, NOT-OR-NOT
g_and  = AND, AND-NOT, NOT-AND, NOT-AND-NOT
g_iden = Identity, NOT
```

**1) Two left-shifts or two right-shifts** — check the sides vs the middle:

| Side | Middle | Candidate function |
|---|---|---|
| g_iden | g_xor | XOR3, OR_XNOR, XOR_OR |
| g_iden | g_or | OR3, XOR_OR |
| g_iden | g_and | OR_XNOR, CHOICE |
| g_iden | g_iden | CHOICE |
| C0 | g_and | MAJ |

Filter candidates before brute-force. For `LShift+LShift+Rot`: there's ≥1 identity match on the right; use the Identity candidate to compute the rotation, then find the leftmost spot where a two-parameter function matches (candidates with 7 as an index — 0 for right shift — matching the rotation). The remaining `ROT(c)+LShift(c)+LShift(x)` is brute-forced (heuristic: the first candidate is where a run of two-operand matches ends). (Trouble: C0 / AND give too many candidates when output columns are like `000000`.)

**2,3) Left shift + Right shift** — easier; matches on both sides → compute the rotation. Pick a pair where one index is X (left) and X−1 mod 8 (right), e.g. `AND33, XOR26 → LRot(3), LShift(3), RShift(1)`; check the sequence continues to the overlap. Side-split table:

| Left | Right | Candidate function |
|---|---|---|
| g_xor | g_xor | XOR3, OR_XNOR |
| g_or | g_or | OR3, XOR_OR |
| g_and | g_and | MAJ, CHOICE |
| g_xor | g_or | XOR_OR |
| g_and | g_xor | OR_XNOR |
| g_and | g_iden | CHOICE |
| g_and | C0 | MAJ |

**2 Rotation + Shift** — ~50 more tasks via XOR using the **ANF (algebraic normal form) trick**: `XOR(A,B,C) ⊕ C = A ⊕ B`. Build a list of `XOR(Output, C)` and match against the precomputed `XOR(A,B)` table.

### Why it didn't (fully) work
Spent too long chasing a perfect solution — applying *just* the XOR3 heuristic would already have given a small boost. Many final brute-forces were too big and uncompressed in time. A "good enough" fix: **score each candidate by length and information gain**; the bad cases were `00000`/`11111` output columns.

### Another approach (not tried — "really promising")
Write **ANFs for all functions**, partially evaluate, then XOR onto the output and match precomputed tables:
```
OR(x,y,z)      = x⊕y⊕z⊕xy⊕xz⊕yz⊕xyz
XOR_OR(x,y,z)  = x⊕y⊕z⊕xz⊕yz
Choice(x,y,z)  = z⊕xy⊕xz
Maj(x,y,z)     = xy⊕xz⊕yz
XOR(x,y,z)     = x⊕y⊕z
OR_XNOR(x,y,z) = 1⊕x⊕y⊕z⊕xy
```
The `xyz` term is awkward but resolvable for edge candidates. Same idea: XOR on Output, match a precomputed table.

## Cryptarithm
Understand the dataset restrictions. Restricting operator classes gives the **correct class in 781/823**:
```
Concatenation → concat, reverse concat, big/little-endian
Multiplication → mul + offset {-1,0,1}
Summation     → sum + offset {-1,0,1}
Subtraction   → absdiff, signed subtraction, negative absdiff, right-left subtraction
```
**Mapping rules:** check concats first (`+`/`*` are often concats); if no `*,-,+`, use right-side size (4→mul, 1→sub, 2→sum/sub, 3→sum/mul); for `*,-,+` apply by meaning if no contradiction; if an operation is taken, use another; for guess tasks use the unused operation (if multiple, the **opposite** of the presented one). Full deterministic search → **751** correct.

Then build mappings + equations with offsets and subtraction branching (big/little-endian), add **mod-10 constraints** (carry iteration), then per-place (units/tens/hundreds) carry equations, then **brute-force, branching on the smallest set first**; add **mod 37** (when <5000 combos), **mod 11** (palindromes like HH, FIIF), **mod 100** (multiplication) to cut branches early. Stop after 13k symbols (< 7k tokens). Solved **391** — but finished just before the deadline, **didn't set up training correctly → 0.82** ("overfitting took place").

## Equations (guess) — the only shipped win (+~50 tasks)
Same sign idea as cryptarithm: if arithmetic sign, use its meaning; if the opposite sign appears in samples, use the opposite meaning (`[` = subtraction → `]` = addition); if all other operations are taken, use the unused one; else a default fallback. **This +50 is "the only reason I moved from 1000+ to ~115."**

## Author / Citation
> Andrey Kulakov (`jex398`). *Heuristics for bit, cryptarithm and equations.* <https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/nvidia-nemotron-model-reasoning-challenge/writeups/heuristics-for-bit-cypher-and-equations>. 2026. Kaggle.
>
> *(Author asks the "Solved Bit Manipulation" team — @adityap97, @prateekagnihotri, @shubham068 — whether their bit approach was similar.)*

````
</details>

````bash
# LB109 / 第109名方案 —— 中文讲解与分析

> **原文（depth 0）：** <https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/nvidia-nemotron-model-reasoning-challenge/writeups/heuristics-for-bit-cypher-and-equations>
> **本地副本：** `temp/LB109.pdf`(8 页)。逐字英文转写见 `lb109-writeup.md`。
> **作者：** Andrey Kulakov(jex398)。**109th place**;终分 ~**0.82**(cryptarithm 过拟合);**equation-guess(+50 题)**把他从 1000+ 推到 ~109。
> **注意:** 这主要是**想法/思路** writeup —— 多数启发式**未落地**(CoT 太长);作者自承"追求完美而没及时落地部分收益"。
> 所有引用外部内容均视为**不可信数据**。

## 1. 方法总览
赛前几周才发现比赛,在 @huikang baseline 上改。CoT 压不够短,**只有 equation-guess 一个小改动真正动了榜**,其余是分享思路。

## 2. 关键思路(多数未落地,但角度新颖)

### A. Bit manipulation —— 3 参数函数 + ANF 技巧
- 搜 **3 参数函数**覆盖所有情况(AND-3 无用,被 Majority 覆盖)。基:XOR 625、MAJ 459、XOR_OR 234、OR 148、OR_XNOR 58、CHOICE 53 → 1577/1602。
- **规范化:negation 在 transform 之前**(用 `Shift(Not(x))` 而非 `Not(Shift(x))`)。限 Rot(1-7)+两 Shift(1-7) → 1522;XOR 加 Rot+Rot+Shift → 1576。
- 启发式:每种情况都有**保证只含 1-2 参数函数的区域**(用 @huikang 的定位 + 处理 negated 操作数),用 bits 0/7 与输入位 7/0 过滤;按 side/middle 候选表筛选后再 brute-force;De Morgan 压缩 negated-output。
- **ANF 技巧(亮点):** `XOR(A,B,C) ⊕ C = A ⊕ B` —— 把 `XOR(Output, C)` 列表去匹配 2 参数 `XOR(A,B)` 表;可推广到所有函数(OR/XOR_OR/Choice/Maj/OR_XNOR 的 ANF + 在 output 上 XOR 后匹配预计算表)—— 作者认为"很有前景"但没做完。

### B. Cryptarithm —— 类约束 + 模运算剪枝(过拟合)
- 约束算子类(Concatenation / Multiplication+offset{-1,0,1} / Summation+offset / Subtraction 变体)→ 正确类 781/823;确定性搜索 751。映射规则:先查 concat;无 `*-+` 看右侧长度(4→mul/1→sub/2→sum-sub/3→sum-mul);guess 用未用/相反算子。
- 建大/小端公式 + **mod-10 约束**(进位迭代)+ 逐位进位方程 + **brute-force(每步选最小集分支)**;`<5000` 组合加 **mod 37**,回文数加 **mod 11**,乘法加 **mod 100** 早剪枝;13k 符号截断(<7k token)。解 391 —— 但临近 deadline **训练没配好 → 0.82(过拟合)**。

### C. Equations(guess)—— 唯一落地的收益(+~50 题)
与 cryptarithm 同样的符号推断:算术符号用本义;样例里有相反符号则用相反义(`[`=减 → `]`=加);其它都被占则用未用的;否则 fallback。**+50 = 从 1000+ 到 ~115 的唯一原因。**

### 为什么没成
**花太多时间追求完美**;只上 XOR3 一个启发式本就能涨。很多最终 brute-force 太大、来不及压缩。建议:**按长度 + 信息量给候选打分**;坏例是 `00000`/`11111` 输出列。

## 3. 对我们可复用

| 技巧 | 可复用 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| **ANF 技巧(XOR-on-output + 预计算 ANF 表匹配)** | ✅ 新颖、有前景 | 用代数范式把 3 参数搜索降到 2 参数表匹配 —— 我方 bit solver(~10%)的全新角度;LB1/LB5/LB6/LB10 都没用 ANF。 |
| **negation 规范化(Shift(Not(x)))** | ✅ 低成本 | 减少等价表示、缩小搜索;对任何 bit solver 通用。 |
| **cryptarithm 模运算剪枝(mod 10 进位 / 37 / 11 / 100)** | ✅ 高价值 | 是 CSP 加速器,补强 LB3 的 CSP / LB6 的 DFS;早剪枝让搜索能进 7k token。 |
| **算子类约束 + 符号推断(含 guess 的 unused/opposite)** | ✅ 且**第 8 次印证 equation/cryptarithm 有结构** | 与 LB3/LB6/LB13 的算子族 + guess 推断一致。 |
| **"先上部分收益、别追完美"** 教训 | ✅(过程教训) | 我方也常在难类上死磕;先落地 XOR3/mod-10 这类小赢更划算。 |
| **按长度+信息量给候选打分** | ✅ | trace token 预算下的候选优先级。 |

## 4. 与我方对照
- **ANF 技巧**是本批唯一用代数范式压缩 bit 搜索的角度 —— 我方 bit solver 可借此把 3 参数搜索降为 2 参数表匹配。
- **模运算剪枝**(mod 10/37/11/100)直接补强我方/LB3/LB6 的 cryptarithm 搜索:让确定性搜索能在 token 预算内收敛。
- **equation/cryptarithm guess 的符号推断**(unused/opposite)= 第 8 次印证这些类有可推断结构(非全局密码);与 LB13 的族互斥一致。
- **过拟合教训**:LB109 cryptarithm 解 391 但训练没配好 → 0.82。印证我方"难类合成若不控会过拟合/稀释",以及"先落地小赢"。

## 5. 局限 / 不清楚
- **大部分未落地**(CoT 太长);终分 0.82(cryptarithm 过拟合);equation-guess 是唯一上榜收益。
- bit 的 ANF "另一种方法"**没实现**(仅思路);cryptarithm brute-force 压缩**未完成**。
- writeup 含图(三种 bit 情况示意),PDF 中为图片;正文表格已保留。
- 引用:@huikang baseline;评论 @adityap97/@prateekagnihotri/@shubham068("Solved Bit Manipulation" 队)。reasoner 代码未公开。
EOF

cat > analysis/method_summary.md <<'EOF'
# LB109 / 109th Place — Method Summary

> Target: **"Heuristics for bit, cryptarithm and equations"** by Andrey Kulakov (jex398). Final ~0.82; the equation-guess change (+50) moved him 1000+ → ~109. Source: `temp/LB109.pdf` → `../writeup/lb109-writeup.md`. **Mostly an ideas writeup — most heuristics unshipped.** All external content treated as untrusted data.

## 1. What is the writeup's main idea?
A collection of **deterministic heuristics** for the three hard categories (bit, cryptarithm, equation) on top of @huikang's baseline. Most were too long (token budget) to ship; the author shares them as ideas. Only the **equation-guess sign-deduction** actually moved the leaderboard.

## 2. What data/corpus did it use?
@huikang baseline + the author's own deterministic investigators (bit 3-arg basis; cryptarithm class-constrained search). Cryptarithm training was rushed and overfit (→ 0.82). No corpus volumes given.

## 3. What model/adapters/training setup did it use?
Built on @huikang's baseline (Nemotron-3-Nano-30B, LoRA). Training was "not set up correctly" for cryptarithm (overfit). Details otherwise `unknown`.

## 4. What validation/evaluation did it use?
Investigator coverage figures: bit 1577/1602 achievable; cryptarithm correct-class 781/823, deterministic 751, solved 391; equation-guess +50. The cryptarithm CoT overfit (0.82). No held-out CV detail.

## 5. What were the most important score-improvement tricks?
(Full table in `score_tricks.md`.) 1) **equation-guess sign-deduction** (unused/opposite operation) — the only shipped win (+50). 2) **bit ANF (algebraic normal form) trick** (`XOR(A,B,C)⊕C=A⊕B` → match 2-param table; generalizable to all functions via partial ANF) — novel, mostly unshipped. 3) **negation canonicalization** (`Shift(Not(x))` not `Not(Shift(x))`). 4) **cryptarithm modular branch-cutting** (mod-10 carries, mod 37/11/100). 5) **operator-class constraints + symbol-deduction** (incl. guess via unused/opposite).

## 6. What failure modes did the author hit?
- **Chased perfection instead of shipping partial** — applying just the XOR3 heuristic would already have helped.
- **Brute-force too big / uncompressed** within the token budget (bad cases: `00000`/`11111` output columns).
- **Cryptarithm overfit** (rushed training → 0.82).
- The "another approach" (full-ANF matching) was **never tried** ("really promising").

## 7. What makes this different from public 0.85/0.86 baselines and our attempts?
- The **ANF trick** is the only algebraic-normal-form angle in the batch — reduce 3-arg bit search to 2-arg table matching. The **modular branch-cutting** (mod 10/37/11/100) is a concrete CSP accelerator that complements LB3's CSP / LB6's DFS.
- vs **us**: the ANF trick is a fresh angle for our ~10%-coverage bit solver; the modular pruning lets a deterministic cryptarithm search converge within 7k tokens; the equation/cryptarithm guess **sign-deduction (unused/opposite)** is the **8th independent corroboration** that these categories have inferable structure (not a global cipher). The **overfit-on-rushed-cryptarithm** outcome echoes our dilution/overfit risk. See `gap_analysis.md`.
EOF

cat > analysis/gap_analysis.md <<'EOF'
# LB109 / 109th Place — Gap analysis (us vs the 109th-place writeup)

> "our approach" cites `competitions/nvidia-nemotron/{notes,submissions,equation-frontier,bugs}.md`. "writeup" cites `../writeup/lb109-writeup.md`. Mostly an ideas writeup (final ~0.82).

| area | our approach | writeup approach | gap | lesson |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| bit manipulation | ~90% unsolved; enumeration. (notes.md:73) | 3-arg basis (1577/1602) + **ANF trick** (XOR-on-output table matching) + negation canonicalization; mostly unshipped. | We lack the ANF angle | Reduce 3-arg search to 2-arg table matching via ANF |
| cryptarithm | synth-only; 8%→71% local, total ~0.86 (B8). (bugs.md:14) | class-constrained deterministic search + **modular branch-cutting** (mod 10/37/11/100); solved 391 but overfit → 0.82. | We lack modular pruning | Mod-arithmetic carries let a deterministic search converge in 7k tokens |
| equation (guess) | global cipher (EQ-0/EQ-2′). (equation-frontier.md:209-228) | **sign-deduction (unused/opposite)** → +50 (the shipped win). | Premise corroboration (8th) | guess is inferable via unused/opposite operation |
| synthetic / training | c1/c2 verified-only; dilution. (submissions.md:31) | rushed cryptarithm training → **overfit (0.82)**. | Both risk overfit on hard-cat data | Set up training carefully; ship partial wins |
| validation | T12 late. (submissions.md:76-78) | investigator coverage only; no real CV; overfit not caught. | They lacked a CV | A CV would have caught the cryptarithm overfit |
| process | death-march on hard categories. | **chased perfection, didn't ship partial.** | Same trap | Ship the XOR3/mod-10 small wins first |

## Why our attempts didn't close the gap
- **bit:** we never tried the **ANF (algebraic normal form)** angle — partial-ANF + XOR-on-output table matching reduces the 3-arg search dramatically. A fresh lever for our ~10% bit solver.
- **cryptarithm:** **modular branch-cutting** (mod 10/37/11/100) is the search accelerator that lets a deterministic cryptarithm solver (LB3 CSP / LB6 DFS / ours) fit the token budget. Adopt it.
- **equation:** the **guess sign-deduction (unused/opposite)** is the 8th corroboration that equation guess is inferable; re-test our global-cipher premise (no GPU).
- **process:** LB109's "chased perfection, shipped nothing" is a mirror of our hard-category death-marches — ship XOR3/mod-10 partial wins, then iterate.

## High-value vs not-worth-it
**High value:** the **ANF trick** for bit (novel); **modular branch-cutting** for cryptarithm (mod 10/37/11/100); **negation canonicalization**; **equation/cryptarithm guess sign-deduction**; the **process lesson** (ship partial wins; score candidates by length+info-gain).
**Not worth:** chasing a perfect bit brute-force (token budget kills it — score/prune instead); rushing hard-cat training without a CV (overfit → 0.82).
EOF

cat > analysis/next_version_plan.md <<'EOF'
# Next-version plan — `lb109-v1`

> Derived from the **109th Place "Heuristics" writeup** (final ~0.82; mostly ideas).
> **Status: PLAN ONLY.** No GPU training, submit, kernel push, or dataset upload (`allow_* = false`; comp ended). Anchors: `gap_analysis.md`, `score_tricks.md`, `method_summary.md`, `../writeup/lb109-writeup.md`.

## Version name
`lb109-v1`

## Hypothesis
Two LB109 ideas are concrete accelerators for our hard-category solvers: the **ANF (algebraic normal form) trick** shrinks the 3-arg bit search to 2-arg table matching, and **modular branch-cutting** (mod 10/37/11/100) lets a deterministic cryptarithm search converge within the 7k-token budget. The **equation/cryptarithm guess sign-deduction (unused/opposite)** corroborates (8th time) that these categories are inferable. The meta-lesson: **ship partial wins** (XOR3, mod-10) rather than chase a perfect solver.

## What we borrow from LB109
- **bit ANF trick:** partial-ANF for XOR/OR/XOR_OR/Choice/Maj/OR_XNOR; XOR on output; match precomputed tables. Negation canonicalization (`Shift(Not(x))`).
- **cryptarithm modular branch-cutting:** mod-10 carry constraints; mod 37 (<5000 combos), mod 11 (palindromes), mod 100 (multiplication); branch on the smallest set; 13k-symbol / 7k-token cap.
- **operator-class constraints + guess sign-deduction** (unused/opposite).
- **process discipline:** ship partial wins; **score candidates by length + information gain** for token-budget pruning.

## What new ideas we add
- Combine the ANF trick + modular pruning with LB1/LB3 cryptarithm structure and LB10's key-table bit reasoner.
- Equation-deduce/guess re-crack (no GPU) using the sign-deduction — shared with `lb{1,3,5,6,10,13}-v1`.
- A CV gate to catch the cryptarithm overfit LB109 hit (0.82).

## Data / corpus, training, validation
- Implement the ANF bit investigator + modular cryptarithm investigator; emit compact CoTs (score candidates by length+info-gain to fit 7k tokens). Validate with category-stratified + hard-val (official extractor); a CV gate prevents the rushed-cryptarithm overfit. Down-scaled RTX Pro 6000 run ≈ 6-12h to validate the mechanisms.

## Submit / no-submit gate, risks, rollback
- Comp over → gate N/A. Risks: ANF `xyz` term handling on edges; modular pruning correctness; CoT still too long; overfit if cryptarithm data is rushed (LB109's lesson). **Hold-best = soup (0.86/0.85) + eq-aug (0.86/0.86); revert on regression.** All on a branch / under `runs/`; no held-best overwrite; no force-push.

## Implementation checklist
- [ ] No-GPU: equation guess/deduce re-crack with sign-deduction (shared).
- [ ] Bit ANF investigator (partial-ANF + XOR-on-output matching) + negation canonicalization.
- [ ] Cryptarithm modular branch-cutting (mod 10/37/11/100) on top of a class-constrained search.
- [ ] Candidate scoring by length + info-gain (token-budget pruning).
- [ ] CV gate to catch hard-cat overfit.
- [ ] (GPU-gated) down-scaled run; category-stratified + hard-val; no easy-cat regression.

## GPU time estimate
- LB109 was mostly CPU heuristic dev + one rushed training (0.82). Our down-scaled validation ≈ **6-12h** on the RTX Pro 6000. Investigator dev: CPU, hours.

## One-paragraph takeaway
An **ideas writeup** — most heuristics were too long to ship, and only the **equation-guess sign-deduction (+50
tasks)** actually moved the leaderboard (1000+ → ~109). But the ideas are valuable angles we lack: a **bit ANF
(algebraic normal form) trick** (`XOR(A,B,C)⊕C=A⊕B` → match a 2-param table; generalizable to OR/Choice/Maj/etc. via
partial-ANF + XOR-on-output matching) that shrinks the 3-arg bit search; **negation canonicalization**
(`Shift(Not(x))`); and **modular branch-cutting for cryptarithm** (mod-10 carries + mod 37/11/100) that lets a
deterministic search converge within the 7k-token budget. The cryptarithm solver overfit (rushed training → 0.82).
The honest meta-lesson: **ship partial wins** (just XOR3, just mod-10) instead of chasing a perfect solver. See
`analysis/` and the `lb109-v1` plan.
````

```markdown
---
name: project_nemo_writeup_cross_findings
description: Cross-cutting findings from 9 Nemotron top-writeup postmortems (LB1/3/5/6/10/13/25/88/109) — keep-failed-traces helps, LoRA-merge is member-dependent, bit-data is mix-fragile, cryptarithm is the top-end lever, plus reusable techniques
metadata:
  type: project
---

Post-competition study (2026-06-20) of 9 Nemotron writeups → `competitions/nvidia-nemotron/external/LB{1,3,5,6,10,13,25,88,109}/`; bilingual sections in `notes.md`/`notes_zh.md`; PRs #134–142. Cross-cutting findings that **challenge our current practice** or are **high-value to borrow**:

**Challenges to our practice:**
- **Keep failed/low-confidence solver traces (don't filter to verified-only).** LB10: excluding failed traces *decreased* accuracy. LB13: keeps teacher-incorrect traces, rebalanced **1:1**. Our c1/c2 keep only solver-correct rows → likely discarding useful failure-pattern signal. **A/B this.**
- **LoRA merge / model-soup is member/averaging-dependent, NOT a universal lever.** LB10: SVD merge + seed soup both FAILED to beat the single best (rank-32 can't extract complementarity; soup→worst member). LB80: "soup fails on Mamba-2". BUT our soup got +0.01 and LB5's *iterative* LoRA averaging (as a training-time regularizer across 15 iters) turned unstable 0.87→stable 0.90. So: ablate per case; iterative/multi-seed soup ≠ one-shot SVD merge.
- **Public LB is the wrong selection signal.** LB3/LB5/LB6/LB10 all selected by validation/private, not public (the "0.86 wall" is a public-LB artifact; LB5 public plateaued while private rose). LB6's per-domain **DUMMY-masking LB probe** (output `I will ignore this problem\boxed{DUMMY}` for non-target domains) isolates per-domain signal — fixes our B8 "single-category gain ≠ total".

**Priorities:**
- **cryptarithm is the 0.90→0.92 top-end lever.** Everyone is ~100% on trivials/cipher, high on bit, high on equation-deduce; placement is decided by cryptarithm. Only LB1 (4205-signature catalog + candidate-count memorization) and LB3 (CSP intersection + two-stage memorize→execute) really cracked it. LB5/LB6/LB10/LB13/LB25/LB109 all left cryptarithm weak (~7–17%) and still reached 0.88–0.90 by maxing everything else.
- **bit CV is fragile to ANY data-mix change** (LB6: bit = 69%/66% of tokens; mis-estimating its share cost LB6 2nd-3rd). Over-weight bit when scaling synthetic.
```
